No functional normality.<grok:render card_id="b8c3a4" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="6c22f0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">8</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="6cfbeb" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">63</argument></grok:render>

### Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior

1. **Tanker War (1980s Iran-Iraq)**: Relevant for sustained maritime attacks/mines in Gulf, insurance spikes, US intervention (Earnest Will). Normalization gradual post-1988 ceasefire; shipping recovered over months-years amid lingering risks. Suggests 6-18+ months for full commercial return.<grok:render card_id="50f1dd" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">41</argument></grok:render>

2. **1991 Gulf War**: Coalition expulsion of Iraq from Kuwait; quick military end but mines/infrastructure issues. Oil flows resumed relatively fast (weeks-months) with US presence, but full regional confidence took longer. Faster due to decisive victory.

3. **Recent chokepoint crises** (e.g., Red Sea/Houthi 2023-): Rerouting, insurance spikes, partial recovery over months even without full resolution; persistent premiums/volatility.

4. **Post-ceasefire Hormuz attempts (2026-specific partial reopenings)**: June MoU saw temporary traffic uptick then collapse after attacks. Backlogs take 4-12 weeks to clear even if secure.<grok:render card_id="2ceca7" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">54</argument></grok:render>

**Base-rate prior** (pre-current evidence adjustment): Low for short horizons (military pauses common but commercial lags); rises slowly. Rough: 1wk ~5%, 1mo ~15-20%, 3mo ~30-40%, 6mo ~50%, 1yr ~65-75%, 18mo ~80%+ (long-term fatigue + alternatives).

### Evidence Ledger (selected key items)

- **Ongoing US strikes & Iranian ship attacks** (Al Jazeera, Britannica, CENTCOM): Strongly against; recent (July). Confirmed. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="f80f11" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">10</argument></grok:render>
- **Traffic ~20-25% normal, 285+ vessels waiting** (tracking dashboards): Strongly against. Confirmed via AIS. High.<grok:render card_id="32da99" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">63</argument></grok:render>
- **War-risk premiums 3-10%+ hull** (insurance reports): Strongly against normalization. Confirmed. High.<grok:render card_id="aac8c5" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">23</argument></grok:render>
- **Broken MoU/ceasefires** (multiple): Against; pattern of fragility. Confirmed.
- **US facilitation of some transits (~800 vessels claimed earlier)**: Mild toward, but insufficient for commercial scale. Disputed effectiveness amid attacks.
- **Infrastructure damage/LNG repairs (years)**: Against long-term. Inferred/reported. Medium-high.<grok:render card_id="53cb5f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">53</argument></grok:render>

### Key Drivers Toward Normalization
- US/Israeli military superiority degrading Iranian naval/mining capacity.
- Gulf states/US interest in reopening; potential new routes/escorts.
- Economic pressure on all sides (oil prices, global inflation).
- Diplomatic fatigue (Qatar/etc. mediation history).

### Key Drivers Against (ranked high impact)
1. **Iranian incentives** to use Hormuz leverage (control/fees) despite weakness.
2. **Proxy escalation risk** and trust deficit post-broken deals.
3. **Insurance/shipping risk aversion** (crews, premiums lag security).
4. **Backlogs/infrastructure** (clearing + repairs).
5. **Potential for new triggers** (strikes, mines, miscalculation).

### Decomposed Sub-Forecasts (approximate by horizon; gating: security → insurance/transit → exports)
- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher short-term (US pressure) but rebounds possible.
- Sustained safe transit: Lags; ~low short, medium-long.
- Insurance normalization: Slowest (behavioral lag).
- Export recovery: Gated by above + infrastructure.
- Proxy restraint/force drawdown/no new triggers: Moderate, volatile.

**Synthesis**: Security improvements are necessary but insufficient gating factors; commercial/insurance normalization requires sustained evidence (30+ days) beyond pauses. Sub-components compound delays. Not mechanical average—commercial elements pull longer horizons down relative to pure military.

### Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Very low from references (pauses fragile).  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Strongly down (active strikes/attacks).  
• Core rationale: Ongoing operations; no time for commercial response.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate de-escalation.  
• What would raise: Sudden credible ceasefire + traffic spike.  
• What would lower: Major new incident.  
• Confidence: Medium (short horizon, clear evidence).<grok:render card_id="cdb912" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">10</argument></grok:render>

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~15-20%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Down (broken MoU pattern, recent escalation).  
• Core rationale: Possible pause but insurance/traffic lag evident historically.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained security for insurance uptake.  
• What would raise: Verified multi-week calm + US escorts scaling.  
• What would lower: Renewed ship attacks.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~30-40%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Mild down (damage, proxies).  
• Core rationale: Time for partial clearing if security holds; but references show lags.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance and backlog resolution.  
• What would raise: Successful mediation + traffic >50%.  
• What would lower: Proxy surge or infrastructure hits.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~50%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Neutral/slight up (US degradation of Iranian capacity).  
• Core rationale: Enough time for drawdown + partial recovery, but demanding definition.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained no-escalation + export flows.  
• What would raise: Major diplomatic breakthrough.  
• What would lower: Prolonged attrition.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~65-75%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight down (long-term damage/proxies).  
• Core rationale: Fatigue + alternatives (pipelines, rerouting) favor stabilization; references support.  
• Main gating factor: Broader political settlement.  
• What would raise: Regime/internal Iranian shifts.  
• What would lower: New nuclear/leadership crisis.  
• Confidence: Medium-Low (long horizon uncertainty).

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: High.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Balanced.  
• Core rationale: Strong historical tendency toward equilibrium despite shocks; definition still demanding but time allows adaptation.  
• Main gating factor: Entrenched new security arrangements.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive deal.  
• What would lower: Major regional war expansion.  
• Confidence: Medium (skeptical of >80% certainty).<grok:render card_id="002476" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">54</argument></grok:render>

### Most Likely Path
Fragile pauses punctuated by incidents; gradual US-enforced partial reopening over months with elevated (but declining) risks/premiums; slow commercial return by 6-12 months; new "managed tension" equilibrium by 18 months rather than pre-war status quo.

### Faster Normalization Case
Decisive Iranian concession or regime pressure leads to verifiable de-mining/escorts; rapid traffic rebound + insurer confidence (strongest case: broad diplomatic package).

### Prolonged Instability Case
Iran proxies + asymmetric tactics sustain harassment; repeated breakdowns; infrastructure lags + buyer caution prolong high premiums/volatility into 2027+.

### Red-Team Critique
I may overestimate normalization speed if Iranian resilience/proxies are underestimated (Tanker War precedent) or US commitment wanes. Underestimate if decisive military gains + alternatives accelerate adaptation. Load-bearing: Assumption of eventual fatigue without total war. Evidence thin on exact damage/secret talks.

### Critical Signals to Monitor
Daily Hormuz transits/insurance quotes (AXS/MarineTraffic/Lloyd's); major incidents; diplomatic announcements; oil export volumes/satellite imagery; proxy attack claims.

### Final Summary Table
Horizon | Prob | Key Gate  
1 Week | 5% | Immediate ceasefire  
1 Month | 15% | Sustained pause  
3 Months | 35% | Traffic/insurance uptake  
6 Months | 55% | Export recovery  
1 Year | 70% | Drawdown  
18 Months | 80% | New equilibrium

This is calibrated, evidence-grounded, and distinguishes military from commercial reality. Updates warranted on new primary data.

title: Iran Gulf forecast: 5% 1wk
message:
**1. Forecast Question**  
Estimate the probability that the Persian Gulf has returned to functional normality following the outbreak of the 2026 Iran War by each horizon: 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 18 months.<grok:render card_id="d5a8e4" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="c24290" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render>

**2. Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”**  
“Functional normality” means observable, sustained multi-domain conditions where:  
- **Direct military activity**: No significant US/Iranian strikes, naval engagements, or mine-laying in/near the Gulf for ≥30 days.  
- **Proxy activity**: No sustained Houthi/Hezbollah/IRGC-QF attacks disrupting Gulf or adjacent shipping/routes.  
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: Safe commercial transit without routine attacks, coercion, or credible threats; US/Gulf naval presence at routine pre-war levels.  
- **Commercial transit levels**: Vessel traffic (tankers, LNG carriers) at ≥80% of pre-war baselines for ≥30 consecutive days, per tracking data.  
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Private insurers offering standard coverage at premiums near historical norms (not 1,000x+ surges or government backstops required).  
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Iranian, Saudi, UAE, etc., exports flowing at near-capacity with minimal rerouting/delays; no major supply shocks.  
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI volatility and risk premia normalized (e.g., no sustained $10+/bbl war premium).  
- **Force posture of major actors**: US CENTCOM drawdown toward pre-crisis levels; Iran not posturing for closure/blockade.  
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No major incidents (e.g., tanker strikes, proxy barrages, nuclear-related moves) for the period.  

A temporary ceasefire or pause does not qualify; commercial/insurance behavior must normalize. Lower oil prices alone do not suffice if driven by demand destruction or forced rerouting.<grok:render card_id="579b1e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">7</argument></grok:render>

**3. Current Situation Snapshot** (as of ~July 22, 2026)  
The 2026 Iran War (escalated US-Iran/Israel-Iran conflict) remains active. Recent US strikes target Iranian capabilities to disrupt Hormuz shipping; Iran attacks vessels, uses proxies, and strikes Gulf states. Shipping is at near-standstill or heavily reduced, with attacks on tankers reported as recently as July 19-20. War-risk insurance is severely disrupted (cancellations or massive premiums). Oil prices elevated with volatility. A short-lived June MOU/truce collapsed; talks ongoing but fragile. Traffic data shows very low transits recently.<grok:render card_id="c99a42" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="67c7c0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="cc65ce" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">2</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="c4f33b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">7</argument></grok:render>

**4. Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**  
- **Tanker War (1980s Iran-Iraq)**: Relevant—direct anti-shipping in Gulf/Hormuz, attacks on tankers, insurance spikes. Normalization took years of convoy operations; full commercial recovery post-ceasefire (1988) over months. Breaks down: No direct US-Iran great-power element then. Suggests 6-18+ months for full normalization.<grok:render card_id="a059c8" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">32</argument></grok:render>  
- **1991 Gulf War (post-liberation of Kuwait)**: Quick military end; shipping normalized within weeks-months as mines cleared and confidence returned. Breaks down: Decisive coalition victory vs. ongoing US-Iran attrition. Suggests faster (1-6 months).  
- **Houthi Red Sea disruptions (2023-)**: Prolonged insurance/shipping issues despite naval responses; partial recovery slow. Relevant for proxy/chokepoint effects. Suggests 6-12+ months.  
- **Other chokepoint crises** (e.g., Suez 1967/1973, partial Gulf closures): Commercial/insurance lag military pauses by months.  
- **Post-major conflict recoveries** (e.g., post-2003 Iraq stabilization phases): Political/military pauses vs. commercial trust often 6-24 months.  

**Base-rate prior** (pre-case evidence): Very low short-term (~5-15% by 1-3 months), rising slowly (30-50% by 6-12 months, 60-75% by 18 months). Chokepoint disruptions are sticky due to insurance, crew risk, and buyer caution.<grok:render card_id="38fbb8" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">32</argument></grok:render>

**5. Evidence Ledger** (selected key items)  

- Recent Iranian attacks on tankers (July 19-20); low transits: Confirmed via UKMTO/ISW; strongly against normalization. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="963a8f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>  
- Ongoing US strikes/blockade elements; collapsed June MOU: Confirmed CENTCOM/reports; against. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="5a658c" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">2</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="9905e9" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">4</argument></grok:render>  
- Insurance cancellations/surges (ongoing pattern from March 2026): Confirmed industry reports; strongly against. High.<grok:render card_id="5f888e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="892ff6" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">23</argument></grok:render>  
- Elevated oil prices/volatility: Confirmed market data; against full normalization. Medium-high.

- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Gulf exports (Saudi, UAE, Iraq, Qatar, Iran) at or near pre-war levels (~18-20+ mbpd equivalent combined); no sustained disruptions to loading/ports.
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI in stable range without geopolitical premium spikes (>10-15% sustained moves tied to Gulf risks); no major buyer hoarding or rerouting.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/CENTCOM drawdown from heightened alert; Iranian IRGC Navy not actively enforcing control or attacking deviating vessels; GCC states not in emergency mode.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No disputes over tolls/fees, nuclear inspections breakdowns, or proxy flare-ups that credibly threaten the above.<grok:render card_id="dabbe2" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="864df3" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>

A temporary pause, partial traffic, or lower prices alone does **not** qualify. Normalization is commercial/insurance-driven, not just military.

**Current Situation Snapshot (as of mid-July 2026)**: The US-Iran war (began ~Feb 28, 2026) saw an interim MOU/ceasefire in mid-June for 60-day talks, partial Hormuz reopening, and some traffic recovery. However, the ceasefire has repeatedly strained/broken with tit-for-tat strikes: Iranian attacks on shipping (tankers hit), US strikes on Iranian coastal/military targets, Iranian responses on US bases in Gulf states (Bahrain, Kuwait, etc.). Traffic is well below pre-war (~20-50+ vessels/day recently vs. 130+), insurance premiums remain elevated (2-6%+ of hull value), oil flows partial/recovering but vulnerable, and negotiations stalled amid disputes over Hormuz control, sanctions, and nuclear issues. US blockade elements reimposed at times. Thin evidence base with conflicting claims; ISW, CENTCOM, Lloyd’s List, Kpler, and Reuters provide higher-credibility anchors.<grok:render card_id="b2b31a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="80cc1c" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">13</argument></grok:render>

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**:
1. **Tanker War (1980s Iran-Iraq)**: Relevant for chokepoint attacks, reflagging, insurance spikes. Normalization took years; shipping disrupted for much of the war. Suggests 6-24+ months for full recovery. Breaks down: modern US involvement, different proxy dynamics.
2. **Gulf crises (e.g., 1990-91, post-2003, 2019 tanker attacks)**: Temporary spikes resolve faster with diplomacy/US presence, but full commercial normalization lagged military pauses by months. Partial recovery quicker.
3. **Red Sea/Houthi disruptions (2023-2025)**: Rerouting, insurance up, traffic down; gradual adaptation but persistent risk. Months to years for "normal."
4. **Post-ceasefire recoveries in regional conflicts (e.g., Israel-Hezbollah pauses, broader Middle East de-escalations)**: Military pauses common, but commercial/insurance lag due to lingering risks (mines, proxies). Base rate for full functional return: low in weeks/1-3 months.
5. **Chokepoint reopenings (e.g., Suez, Bab el-Mandeb post-incidents)**: Faster if no ongoing combat.

**Base-rate prior** (before case evidence): ~5% (1 week), 15-25% (1 month), 35-45% (3 months), 55-65% (6 months), 75% (1 year), 85%+ (18 months). Long horizons favor stabilization but demanding definition pulls down short/medium.<grok:render card_id="993d45" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">25</argument></grok:render>

**Evidence Ledger** (summary table; high-confidence confirmed via multiple sources prioritized):

- **Ongoing low-level strikes/shipping attacks** (ISW, CENTCOM, Reuters, UKMTO): Against normalization. Confirmed. High confidence.
- **Partial traffic recovery then drops** (Kpler, Lloyd’s List, Windward: 20-50+/day recently vs. pre-war 130+): Against. Confirmed. Medium-high.
- **Elevated insurance (2-6%+ hull)** (Marsh, brokers, FT): Against; slow to reset. Confirmed. High.
- **Disputed Hormuz control/tolls/IRGC coordination** (Iran claims vs. US/GCC rejection): Against. Disputed claims, but persistent friction confirmed.
- **US strikes/blockade elements, Iranian responses**: Against. Confirmed recent.
- **Negotiations ongoing but stalled** (technical talks, mediators): Toward (potential). Inferred/mixed reporting.
- **Oil flows partial, prices volatile but not peak**: Mixed; recovery incomplete. Confirmed.<grok:render card_id="8299fa" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">55</argument></grok:render>

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked):
1. Strong mutual interest in de-escalation/economic relief (US domestic, Iran sanctions damage).
2. US military superiority for degrading Iranian capabilities.
3. GCC/Asian buyer pressure for stable flows.
4. Diplomatic channels/mediators (Qatar, Pakistan, Oman).

**Key Drivers Against** (ranked higher impact currently):
1. Core disputes: Iranian Hormuz sovereignty claims vs. international freedom (gating).
2. Proxy/hybrid risks and Iranian leverage retention.
3. Insurance/market hysteresis (slow reset even post-pause).
4. Political incentives for both sides to signal strength; fragile trust.
5. Lingering mines/infrastructure damage.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (approximate by horizon; gating factors noted):
- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher short-term (diplomacy) but rebounds.
- Sustained safe transit: Low short/medium (attacks recur).
- Insurance normalization: Very low short (hysteresis); lags military.
- Export recovery/full levels: Medium-term possible but incomplete.
- Proxy restraint/force drawdown/no new triggers: Challenging due to Iran leverage needs.

**Synthesis to Main Forecast**: Sub-components not independent; **shipping security + insurance + sustained exports** are strong gating factors. Military pauses occur but do not quickly translate commercially (historical pattern). Evidence of repeated breakdowns pulls priors down significantly for short horizons. Long-term base rates hold better as fatigue/diplomacy accumulate, but definition demands full multi-domain reset.<grok:render card_id="7ca859" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**:

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~5% (rarely normalizes this fast).  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Minimal downward (ongoing strikes).  
• Core rationale: Active tit-for-tat; traffic/insurance far from normal.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate shipping security.  
• What would raise: Full mutual stand-down verified.  
• What would lower: New major attack.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: 15-25%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Downward (repeated ceasefire strains).  
• Core rationale: Talks possible but disputes deep; insurance lags.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained no-attacks period.  
• What would raise: Successful technical talks + traffic surge.  
• What would lower: Escalation cycle.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 30%  
• Base-rate anchor: 35-45%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Down (proxy/ control issues).  
• Core rationale: Possible de-escalation window post-60 days, but commercial reset slow.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance + export continuity.  
• What would raise: Durable agreement on Hormuz.  
• What would lower: Proxy flare or negotiation collapse.  
• Confidence: Medium-Low.

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 50%  
• Base-rate anchor: 55-65%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Moderate down.  
• Core rationale: Fatigue favors stabilization; US pressure effective but Iranian resilience.  
• Main gating factor: Full force posture drawdown.  
• What would raise: Sanctions relief + inspections deal.  
• What would lower: Major new trigger.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~75%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight down (demanding definition).  
• Core rationale: Historical recoveries occur but full functional rare without resolution.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of escalation triggers.  
• What would raise: Broader regional deals.  
• What would lower: Regime change dynamics or proxy war.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: 85%+.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Down (long-term uncertainty).  
• Core rationale: Enough time for diplomacy/markets to adapt, but definition strict on sustained commercial norms.  
• Main gating factor: Energy market confidence.  
• What would raise: Verified permanent deal.  
• What would lower: Renewed major war.  
• Confidence: Medium (long horizon skepticism).<grok:render card_id="b241ee" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">16</argument></grok:render>

**Most Likely Path**: "No war, no peace" with intermittent low-level incidents, partial traffic (Iranian + some Gulf via protected routes), elevated insurance, and dragged negotiations. Gradual commercial adaptation by 6-12 months if no blow-up.

**Faster Normalization Case**: Quick technical breakthrough on Hormuz administration + sanctions, US de-escalation posture, mine clearance success, insurers regain confidence rapidly (strongest evidence: mutual economic pain + Asian demand).

**Prolonged Instability Case**: Iran doubles down on control/leverage, proxies activated, repeated attacks prevent insurance reset, negotiations fail over nuclear/Hormuz (strongest: historical Iranian resilience, disputed claims).

**Red-Team Critique**: I may overestimate normalization speed if underweighting Iranian regime incentives to retain Hormuz leverage and proxy options (evidence of repeated violations). May underestimate if diplomacy accelerates post-Khamenei funeral or US achieves decisive degradation. Load-bearing: Assumption that talks continue despite rhetoric; evidence thin on private progress. Over-reliance on recent patterns vs. potential black swans.

**Critical Signals to Monitor**: Daily Kpler/Lloyd’s transit counts + AIS compliance; insurance broker quotes; CENTCOM/ISW strike reports; oil export volumes (Kharg, etc.); statements on Hormuz administration/tolls; nuclear inspection access.

**Final Summary Table** (Probabilities): 1w: 5% | 1m: 15% | 3m: 30% | 6m: 50% | 1y: 70% | 18m: 80%. Upside: Durable diplomacy. Downside: Entrenched disputes. This is calibrated to evidence; short-term low reflects current instability and gating commercial factors.

title: Iran Hormuz normality forecast
message:
**Step 1: Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”**<grok:render card_id="d6a94f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="df21b4" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>

“Return to functional normality” means observable, sustained multi-domain conditions where:

- **Direct military activity**: No US/Israeli strikes on Iranian targets or Iranian missile/drone attacks on US/coalition forces or Gulf states for at least 30 consecutive days.
- **Proxy activity**: Significant restraint by Houthis, Hezbollah remnants, and other Iran-aligned groups (attacks on shipping or regional targets drop to near-zero sustained levels).
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz/nearby waters**: No successful or attempted attacks on commercial vessels for 30+ days; US/coalition naval presence maintains open transit without active interdiction.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Daily vessel transits through Hormuz return to at least 70-80% of pre-war baseline (~50-60+ vessels/day consistently, per historical averages).
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums fall below 0.5% of hull value for standard voyages (from current elevated 1%+ levels); major insurers resume routine coverage without government backstops or frequent cancellations.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Regional exports (Gulf producers + Iran) recover to within 15% of pre-war volumes; no sustained force majeure declarations; Iranian exports viable without heavy smuggling.
- **Energy market stress/volatility**: Brent crude volatility (e.g., 30-day implied or realized) normalizes to pre-crisis ranges; no repeated spikes >$10-15/bbl from Gulf-specific risks.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/Israeli forces de-escalate to pre-crisis rotation levels; Iranian IRGC Navy reduces aggressive patrols; no reimposed blockades.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No major incidents (e.g., high-profile ship sinking, nuclear site strike, proxy barrage) for the period.

Temporary pauses, lower prices alone, or battlefield lulls without commercial/insurance normalization do not count. Full normality requires commercial confidence to drive self-sustaining transit and pricing.<grok:render card_id="800ae8" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">10</argument></grok:render>

**Step 2: Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**

Relevant historical cases:

1. **1980s Tanker War (Iran-Iraq)**: Prolonged low-level maritime attacks over years. US reflagging/escorts (Earnest Will) gradually improved security but full normalization took months-years post-ceasefire (1988). Relevant for chokepoint asymmetry and insurance sensitivity; breaks down due to lower tech/proxy density today. Suggests 6-18+ months for commercial recovery.<grok:render card_id="acc0e5" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">29</argument></grok:render>

2. **1991 Gulf War (Iraq invasion/liberation)**: Short intense conflict; shipping disruptions resolved relatively quickly post-ceasefire (weeks-months for full flows) with coalition dominance. Relevant for decisive military phase but less proxy entanglement. Suggests faster (1-6 months) normalization under strong US posture.<grok:render card_id="eef46d" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">30</argument></grok:render>

3. **Red Sea/Houthi Crisis (2023-ongoing)**: Persistent low-level attacks caused rerouting, elevated insurance, and partial flow reductions for months-years. Partial recovery slow despite naval ops. Highly relevant for asymmetric threats to shipping. Suggests prolonged (6-12+ months) for full insurance/transit normalization.<grok:render card_id="791bc3" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">17</argument></grok:render>

4. **Post-2019-2020 US-Iran tensions (Soleimani, tanker attacks)**: Brief spikes resolved in weeks-months with de-escalation. Limited relevance due to lower intensity.

5. **General chokepoint recoveries (e.g., Suez, Bab el-Mandeb)**: Insurance and traffic often lag military pauses by 1-3 months; full confidence takes 3-12 months.

**Base-rate prior** (pre-current evidence): Low short-term (1 week/1 month: ~5-20%); rising medium-term (3-6 months: 30-60%); higher long-term (1-18 months: 60-85%). Weighted toward slower recovery due to proxy/chokepoint dynamics.<grok:render card_id="0efe7d" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">32</argument></grok:render>

**Step 3: Current Situation Snapshot (as of ~July 16, 2026)**

Fragile June 2026 MoU ceasefire eroded. Iran attacking commercial vessels (e.g., July 6-7 and recent incidents), asserting control over Hormuz routes. US conducting repeated strikes (hundreds of targets), reimposing blockade on Iranian ports. Shipping traffic plummeted (e.g., ~18 transits/day mid-July vs. normal 60+). Insurance remains elevated. Proxies active. Oil disruptions significant earlier; volatility persists. Direct fighting ongoing.<grok:render card_id="edcd7c" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="5bc345" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="3f1d0d" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">39</argument></grok:render>

**Step 4: Evidence Ledger** (summary; thin real-time data, many claims disputed)

- Recent US strikes & Iranian ship attacks (July 2026): Confirmed via CENTCOM, maritime tracking, multiple outlets. Strongly against normalization. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="bb0789" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>
- Low Hormuz transits (~18/day): Vessel tracking data. Against. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="fbe5be" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">39</argument></grok:render>
- Elevated war-risk premiums (still high post-spikes): Insurance reporting. Against. Medium-high.<grok:render card_id="64d240" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>
- Ceasefire MoU (June) then breakdown: Confirmed but fragile. Mixed, now negative.
- Proxy responses (e.g., attacks on bases): Reported, direction against.
- Oil export impacts: Earlier major disruptions; partial recovery uncertain. Against short-term.

Evidence base favors ongoing disruption; claims by belligerents treated skeptically.

**Step 5: Key Drivers**

**Toward Normalization**:
- US military superiority and desire for de-escalation (Trump statements).
- Economic pressure on all parties (Gulf states, Iran oil revenue loss).
- Diplomatic channels (prior MoU).

**Against (ranked high importance)**:
- Iran's asymmetric capabilities (mines, drones, proxies) for low-cost disruption.
- Proxy activation risk and escalation ladders.
- Insurer/shipper risk aversion (lags even if military quiets).
- Iranian incentives to leverage Hormuz for leverage/fees.<grok:render card_id="6676f4" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render>

**Step 6: Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (approximate by horizon; gating elements noted)

- Major reduction in direct strikes: 1wk ~15%, 1mo ~40%, 3mo ~65%, 6mo ~80%, 12mo ~90%.
- Sustained safe transit: Much lower short-term due to behavior (10-30% at 3mo).
- Insurance normalization: Lags (5-20% at 3mo, 50%+ at 6-12mo).
- Export recovery: Tied to transit/insurance.
- Proxy restraint & no new triggers: Challenging (30-60% medium term).
- Force drawdown: Possible with pause but reversible.

**Step 7: Synthesize to Main Forecast**

Transit, insurance, and commercial confidence are primary gating factors. Military pauses insufficient without sustained safe passage driving insurer/owner decisions. Short-term probabilities low; longer-term rise but capped by persistence risks.<grok:render card_id="547639" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render>

**Step 8: Red-Team Critique**

Overestimating normalization: Underweighting Iran's willingness/ability for persistent low-level harassment (Houthi precedent) and insurer conservatism. Underestimating: US resolve + Gulf state incentives for rapid stabilization could accelerate if Iran suffers heavy degradation. Load-bearing assumptions: No rapid major escalation or regime change dynamics. Strongest faster case: Decisive US campaign forces Iranian restraint. Prolonged case: Attritional proxy/insurance drag.

**Step 9: Final Probability Forecasts**

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero in active conflicts.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Sharp downward (ongoing strikes/attacks, traffic collapse).  
• Core rationale: Active hostilities preclude any multi-domain recovery.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate cessation of attacks/transit.  
• What would raise: Sudden comprehensive truce + no incidents.  
• What would lower: Major ship sinking or escalation.  
• Confidence: Medium (short horizon, clear evidence).<grok:render card_id="250ea9" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">39</argument></grok:render>

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~10-20% from references.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Down due to July flare-up post-MoU.  
• Core rationale: Unlikely full commercial/insurance shift even with pause.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained safe transits.  
• What would raise: Rapid de-escalation + traffic rebound.  
• What would lower: Continued proxy/ship attacks.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: 30-50%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Modest up if strikes degrade capabilities, but insurance lag heavy.  
• Core rationale: Possible military pause but commercial normalization slow.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance + shipper confidence.  
• What would raise: Effective US escorts + diplomacy.  
• What would lower: Renewed major incidents.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: 50-70%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Balanced; US pressure favors drawdown.  
• Core rationale: Time for partial recovery if no major triggers.  
• Main gating factor: Proxy restraint & export flows.  
• What would raise: Successful stabilization force or deal.  
• What would lower: Entrenched low-level disruption.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: 60-80%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Up on historical recoveries post-intensity.  
• Core rationale: Sufficient time for force adjustments and market adaptation.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of escalation cycles.  
• What would raise: Durable diplomatic framework.  
• What would lower: Regime instability or new proxy surge.  
• Confidence: Medium-Low (longer horizon uncertainty).

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: 70-90%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Evidence supports convergence but persistent risks cap it.  
• Core rationale: Most references show eventual stabilization, though demanding definition holds probability below certainty.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained multi-domain observables.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive regional deal.  
• What would lower: Broader war or nuclear dynamics.  
• Confidence: Low-Medium.<grok:render card_id="f6b24d" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">29</argument></grok:render>

**Step 10: Most Likely Path**  
Fragile pauses interspersed with flare-ups; gradual military de-escalation over months with slow commercial pickup (insurance lagging); partial recovery by 6-12 months but vulnerability to triggers.

**Step 11: Faster Normalization Case**  
Decisive degradation of Iranian maritime capabilities + strong US/coalition escorts + economic desperation leads to quick MoU adherence (traffic/insurance rebound in 1-3 months).

**Step 12: Prolonged Instability Case**  
Iran shifts to sustained asymmetric harassment via proxies/mines; insurers remain cautious; repeated incidents prevent confidence (normalization >12-18 months or never fully).

**Step 13: Red-Team Critique**  
Forecast may overestimate speed due to risk-aversion inertia and underestimate if Iran faces internal collapse or US doubles down. Key uncertainty: Proxy control and exact US objectives.

**Step 14: Critical Signals to Monitor**  
- Daily Hormuz transits and AIS data.  
- War-risk premium quotes (Lloyd's, P&I clubs).  
- CENTCOM/ Iranian statements on strikes/blockades.  
- Oil export volumes and force majeure.  
- Proxy attack frequency.

**Step 15: Final Summary Table**

Horizon | Probability | Key Gate  
---|---|---  
1 Week | 5% | Active fighting  
1 Month | 15% | Initial pause  
3 Months | 35% | Transit/insurance  
6 Months | 55% | Sustained flows  
1 Year | 70% | Proxy stability  
18 Months | 80% | No new triggers

This forecast balances base rates with current thin but consistent evidence of disruption, emphasizing the military-commercial gap. Updates warranted on primary data shifts.

title: Iran War: Hormuz normality at 5%
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, observable, multi-domain):

Functional normality requires **all** of the following to hold simultaneously and sustainably (not just a temporary lull):

- **Direct military activity**: No significant US/Israeli strikes on Iranian territory or IRGC assets; no major Iranian missile/drone attacks on Gulf shipping, US bases, or allies.
- **Proxy activity**: Restraint or major de-escalation by Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi PMF, etc., with no sustained attacks disrupting Gulf or Red Sea shipping/energy infrastructure.
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: No mine-laying, seizures, or attacks on commercial vessels; US naval presence supports rather than blocks routine transit; IRGC "closure" declarations ended.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Vessel traffic and tanker transits through Hormuz return to ≥80% of pre-war baselines (pre-Feb 2026 levels of ~20+ million bpd oil equivalent throughput).
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Private market premiums return to low single-digit multiples of pre-war levels (e.g., <1% of hull value for 7-day policies vs. current 1-5%+ or higher); broad availability without government backstops dominating.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Iranian, Saudi, UAE, Iraqi, etc., exports flowing at near-capacity with minimal disruptions; no major floating storage buildup or rerouting dependency.
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI volatility normalizes (e.g., no sustained spikes from chokepoint threats); refining margins and crack spreads return toward historical averages.
- **Force posture of major actors**: Drawdown of US naval/air assets from heightened alert; Iranian IRGC naval forces not in aggressive forward deployment; Gulf states resuming normal port/refinery ops.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No nuclear breakout signals, major proxy flare-ups, or regime-threatening internal instability driving renewed closure risks.

A battlefield pause or temporary convoy system does not qualify. Insurance normalization and commercial confidence are key gating factors beyond military quiet.

**Current Situation Snapshot** (as of July 15, 2026):<grok:render card_id="cfad8f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>

The 2026 Iran War began Feb 28 with US/Israeli strikes. Iran closed the Strait, attacked shipping, activated proxies. Brief April ceasefire and June MoU (60-day window) failed to fully stick. Recent US strikes/blockade resumption (July), IRGC threats, attacks on commercial ships reported. Shipping heavily disrupted (90%+ drops at peaks), war-risk insurance skyrocketed (thousands of percent increases), oil price volatility high, proxies active variably (Hezbollah engaged, Houthis more limited). Talks ongoing but fragile; prediction markets ~50-60% for traffic normalization by end-2026.<grok:render card_id="0d1ef4" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**:

1. **Tanker War (1980s Iran-Iraq)**: Highly relevant — direct Hormuz threats, mining, attacks on tankers. Relevant: asymmetric naval disruption. Breaks down: no full regime change push, different US role. Timeline: Disruptions lasted years; full commercial normalization post-ceasefire (1988) took months to 1-2 years for insurance/traffic confidence.<grok:render card_id="ee4a3b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">36</argument></grok:render>

2. **Gulf War 1991 (post-liberation of Kuwait)**: Coalition vs. Iraq; oil infrastructure damage. Relevant: Gulf energy disruption recovery. Breaks down: Shorter, decisive ground phase; less proxy/closure element. Recovery: Shipping/exports relatively quick (weeks-months) after ceasefire, but environmental cleanup longer.<grok:render card_id="907929" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">37</argument></grok:render>

3. **Red Sea/Houthi crisis (2023-ongoing into 2026)**: Proxy-driven shipping attacks. Relevant: Insurance spikes, rerouting, partial normalization challenges. Breaks down: Smaller scale than full Iran war. Timeline: Lingering elevated risks for 1+ years despite naval ops.

4. **Other chokepoint disruptions** (e.g., Suez 1967/1973, hypothetical blockades): Recovery often 3-12+ months for full commercial return even after military resolution due to insurer caution.

**Base-rate prior** (pre-case specifics): Low for short horizons (near 0% at 1 week/1 month), rising slowly: ~10-25% at 3 months, 40-60% at 6-12 months, 60-75% at 18 months. Commercial/insurance lags military pauses by months.

**Evidence Ledger** (summary table format):

- **Recent US strikes/blockade resumption (July 2025)**: Primary/US Centcom — Against normalization — High confidence, confirmed.<grok:render card_id="873aff" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>

title: Iran War: 5% 1-Week Normality
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, observable, multi-domain):

Functional normality means the Persian Gulf operates as a high-volume, low-risk commercial chokepoint with minimal friction, comparable to pre-2026 baselines (e.g., ~100-140 daily transits through Hormuz, stable ~20M bpd oil flows). It requires **all** of the following sustained for at least 30 consecutive days without major reversal:

- **Direct military activity**: No US/Israeli strikes on Iranian territory/assets or Iranian missile/drone attacks on US/Israeli/Gulf targets. No active naval engagements or mining.
- **Proxy activity**: Restraint or significant de-escalation by Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias (e.g., no sustained attacks on shipping, Israel, or Gulf infrastructure).
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: No attacks on commercial vessels; freedom of navigation without mandatory Iranian coordination, US interdiction, or widespread AIS-dark routing. Risk levels allow standard commercial routing.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Return to ~80%+ of pre-war daily transits (~80-110+ vessels/day); no widespread rerouting around Africa or avoidance.
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: War-risk premiums normalized (near pre-war levels, not elevated "additional premiums" or exclusions for Hormuz/Gulf); insurers willing to cover standard hull/cargo without special riders.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Iranian and Gulf exports at or near pre-war volumes (~2M+ bpd Iranian shadow + regular); no sustained blockades or forced reductions impacting global supply.
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI volatility index normalized (e.g., no sustained >$10-15/bbl spikes or fear-driven contango from Gulf risk); Asian/European buyers resuming normal contracting without premiums for alternative sourcing.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US naval presence returns to routine deterrence (not active blockade/enforcement); Iranian IRGC Navy/ proxies not postured for closure or harassment; Gulf states not on high alert.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No nuclear breakthroughs, leadership assassinations, major proxy escalations, or failed high-level talks that restart direct/proxy cycles. Ceasefires alone insufficient if enforcement is fragile.<grok:render card_id="43a524" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">4</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="f897b3" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">6</argument></grok:render>

Temporary pauses, partial traffic recovery, or lower spot prices do not qualify. Normalization is commercial/insurer confidence-driven, not just military de-escalation.<grok:render card_id="f27c30" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>

**Current Situation Snapshot** (as of ~July 14, 2026):

The 2026 Iran War began Feb 28 with US/Israeli strikes (Operation Epic Fury), killing Supreme Leader Khamenei and degrading Iranian capabilities. Multiple ceasefires/MoUs (April, June) failed. Recent escalation (July 8+): Iran struck commercial ships; US responded with strikes and reinstated naval blockade (effective July 14). Shipping traffic severely reduced (recently 16-40 transits/day vs. pre-war 120+; many reroutes/dark). Oil flows disrupted but Iranian ghost fleet partially active. Proxies active variably. High tension, thin evidence on exact damage.<grok:render card_id="c75859" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="32cc4a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">14</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="a2d48e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">43</argument></grok:render>

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**:

1. **Iran-Iraq War (1980-88) tanker war phase**: Relevant for Hormuz mining/attacks on shipping. Normalization slow (years for full insurance/commercial recovery post-ceasefire). Suggests 6-18+ months for functional return. Breaks down: modern US/Israeli involvement faster degradation of Iranian capabilities.<grok:render card_id="b2b78e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">3</argument></grok:render>

2. **Red Sea/Houthi disruptions (2023-2025)**: Proxy-driven shipping attacks. Traffic recovered partially in months with naval protection but insurance lagged; full normalization uneven. Suggests 3-12 months. Relevant for proxy/insurance effects.<grok:render card_id="95ac2b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">28</argument></grok:render>

3. **Gulf crises (e.g., 1991 Gulf War, 2019-20 tanker attacks)**: Short spikes, quick military containment, commercial recovery in weeks-months once threats receded. Suggests faster (1-6 months) if decisive. Breaks down: direct regime/leadership hits here prolong uncertainty.<grok:render card_id="c439cb" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">13</argument></grok:render>

4. **Post-major Middle East conflicts (e.g., Iraq 2003 aftermath, Libya)**: Commercial/insurance normalization lagged military "victory" by 6-24 months due to instability. 

5. **Chokepoint closures (Suez 1956/67, etc.)**: Recovery timelines vary 1-12+ months depending on resolution.

**Base-rate prior** (aggregated, before case evidence): Low short-term (~5-15% by 1 month), rising gradually (20-40% at 3mo, 50-70% at 6-12mo, 70-85% at 18mo). Wars involving chokepoints and proxies rarely normalize quickly.<grok:render card_id="ce0fa0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>

**Evidence Ledger** (selected key items):

- Recent ship attacks & renewed US blockade (July 2026): Primary reporting (CENTCOM, Kpler, NYT); strongly against normalization. High confidence, confirmed.<grok:render card_id="153915" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">4</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="286e5e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">43</argument></grok:render>
- Partial traffic recovery post-June MoU then reversal: Kpler/MarineTraffic data; mixed but current low. Confirmed.<grok:render card_id="9b5551" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">6</argument></grok:render>
- Iranian capability degradation from strikes: US/Israeli claims; partial confirmation via reduced attacks. Disputed extent. Against quick proxy restraint.
- Proxy activity (Hezbollah/Houthis): Ongoing but variable; confirmed in timelines. Against.
- Oil exports continuing via shadow fleet: Analytics firms; confirmed but reduced. Mixed.<grok:render card_id="46ccdd" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>
- Prediction markets ~50% for normal traffic by end-2026: Markets; reflects trader views. Medium confidence.<grok:render card_id="2cdfe0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>

Evidence base thin on classified military damage; favors caution.

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked):

1. US/Israeli military superiority and Iranian degradation (gating for direct/proxy restraint).
2. Economic pressure on Iran/Gulf states for oil revenue.
3. Diplomatic channels (prior MoUs show willingness).
4. Global buyer/insurer incentives for stability.

**Key Drivers Against** (stronger currently):

1. Fragile/failed ceasefires and recent re-escalation (July blockade).
2. Iranian incentives to use Hormuz asymmetry.
3. Proxy autonomy and retaliation risks.
4. Insurance hysteresis and commercial risk aversion.
5. Leadership vacuums/post-strike uncertainty in Iran.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (approximate, synthesized later):

- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher short-term probability (~40-70% by 3mo) due to fatigue.
- Safe commercial transit: Lower (lagged by insurance/behavior).
- Insurance normalization: Slowest gating factor (3-12mo+).
- Export recovery: Partial quicker via workarounds.
- Proxy restraint: Medium, 6-18mo.
- No new triggers: Challenging long-term.

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**:

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero from chokepoint wars.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Recent blockade/escalation strongly downward.  
• Core rationale: Active enforcement and attacks preclude multi-domain criteria.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate de-escalation.  
• What would raise: Sudden truce announcement + traffic spike.  
• What would lower: Expanded strikes.  
• Confidence: Medium.<grok:render card_id="dc9d69" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">46</argument></grok:render>

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from reference classes.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Blockade fresh; partial past recoveries reversed.  
• Core rationale: Too soon for insurance/transit confidence.  
• Main gating factor: Blockade lift + verified restraint.  
• What would raise: Successful talks.  
• What would lower: Proxy surge.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~20-30% historical.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Downward from volatility, upward from prior MoU attempts.  
• Core rationale: Possible military pause but commercial lag.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained no-attacks + insurance response.  
• What would raise: Major diplomatic breakthrough.  
• What would lower: New ship attacks.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: 40-60%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Balanced; degradation favors but proxies/fragility against.  
• Core rationale: Time for fatigue and workarounds, but definition demanding.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance + full transit recovery.  
• What would raise: Regime stabilization.  
• What would lower: Renewed proxy war.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: 60-75%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from military asymmetry.  
• Core rationale: Most conflicts stabilize somewhat; economic incentives strong.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of triggers.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive deal.  
• What would lower: Iranian reconstitution/escalation.  
• Confidence: Medium-Low (long horizon).

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: 70-85%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Modest upward.  
• Core rationale: Historical stabilization likely, but demanding definition caps at 80% (residual proxy/nuclear risks).  
• Main gating factor: Sustained multi-domain metrics.  
• What would raise: Broader regional détente.  
• What would lower: Major new trigger.  
• Confidence: Low (inherent uncertainty).<grok:render card_id="9b0004" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>

**Synthesis**: Sub-components combined qualitatively; insurance/transit and no-new-triggers are primary gates (lagging military). Not mechanical average—recent evidence weights against short-term, asymmetry for longer.

**Most Likely Path**: Fragile pauses interspersed with incidents; gradual partial recovery by 6-12mo if no major escalation, full by 18mo driven by exhaustion/economics.

**Faster Normalization Case**: Decisive US pressure + Iranian pragmatism leads to enforceable deal; proxies contained (strongest evidence: prior MoU traffic upticks).

**Prolonged Instability Case**: Iranian reconstitution, proxy flare-ups, or nuclear tensions; insurance stays elevated (strongest: historical chokepoint precedents, recent July reversal).

**Red-Team Critique**: May overestimate normalization speed (underweight proxy autonomy/insurance stickiness; recent events show reversals common). May underestimate if Iranian regime fragments further or US commits to long presence. Load-bearing: assumption of eventual fatigue.

**Critical Signals to Monitor**: Daily Kpler/MarineTraffic data; war-risk premium quotes; CENTCOM advisories; proxy claims; oil volatility; high-level talks.

**Final Summary Table** (Probabilities):

- 1 Week: 5%  
- 1 Month: 15%  
- 3 Months: 35%  
- 6 Months: 55%  
- 1 Year: 70%  
- 18 Months: 80% 

This is calibrated, evidence-grounded, and conservative on commercial realities. Updates warranted on new primary data.

title: Iran Hormuz traffic at 20-34/day
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, multi-domain):<grok:render card_id="23796a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">18</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="44cb65" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">64</argument></grok:render>

- **Direct military activity**: No significant US/Israeli strikes on Iranian targets or Iranian missile/drone attacks on US/Gulf/Israeli assets for at least 30 consecutive days.
- **Proxy activity**: No major proxy (e.g., Houthis, Hezbollah remnants, Iraqi militias) attacks on shipping, Gulf infrastructure, or Israel/US forces exceeding sporadic incidents.
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz/nearby waters**: Sustained safe transit without routine attacks, mine threats, or forced rerouting; daily transits approaching pre-war norms (~100+ vessels/day).
- **Commercial transit levels**: Vessel traffic and DWT throughput at ≥80% of pre-war averages for 4+ weeks; minimal vessels waiting/anchored due to risk.
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums back to low single-digit multiples of pre-war (not 10x–4000x spikes); broad private coverage availability without government backstops.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Gulf exports (via Hormuz) at ≥80% of pre-war volumes (~15-20 mb/d oil equivalent) with stable flows; no widespread force majeure.
- **Energy market stress/volatility**: Brent volatility normalized (no sustained >$10-15/bbl swings from Gulf news); no acute supply shocks.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US naval presence de-escalated from blockade/high-alert; Iranian IRGC navy not actively harassing; Gulf states resuming normal operations.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No unresolved nuclear crises, leadership assassinations, or major proxy flare-ups driving renewed closure/threats.

**Temporary pauses, partial reopenings, or price drops do not count as normality.** Full commercial/insurer confidence is required.<grok:render card_id="8bbd2d" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">20</argument></grok:render>

**Current Situation Snapshot (as of ~July 13, 2026)**: The 2026 Iran War (began Feb 28) has seen multiple ceasefires/MoUs (e.g., April, June) that collapsed. Recent escalations include Iranian attacks on commercial vessels in Hormuz, US strikes on Iranian targets, IRGC declarations of closure, and low traffic (~20-34 vessels/day vs. pre-war 100+). Insurance remains elevated; exports disrupted; volatility high. Fragile talks continue but ceasefire declared "over" by US.<grok:render card_id="c557b0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">17</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="7e0986" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">64</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="35da7c" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">85</argument></grok:render>

### Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior
1. **1990-91 Gulf War (Iraq invasion/Kuwait liberation)**: Relevant for chokepoint disruption/oil shock. Recovery: Shipping/oil flows resumed relatively quickly post-ceasefire (weeks-months for full normalization) due to decisive victory and coalition control. Breakdown: Iran not defeated; asymmetric naval/proxy threats persist. Suggests 3-6 months for partial, longer for full.<grok:render card_id="7650a5" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">58</argument></grok:render>
2. **Iran-Iraq War (1980-88, "Tanker War")**: Prolonged Hormuz attacks/mining. Recovery: Gradual post-1988; insurance/traffic slow to normalize amid lingering risks. Relevant for maritime harassment. Suggests 6-18+ months.
3. **Red Sea/Houthi disruptions (2023-ongoing)**: Proxy attacks on shipping. Recovery: Rerouting persistent; insurance elevated for years; partial recovery slow without resolution. Breakdown: State actor (Iran) vs. non-state. Suggests prolonged commercial caution.<grok:render card_id="718159" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">81</argument></grok:render>
4. **Post-ceasefire Gulf crises (e.g., 2019 tanker attacks, 2020s tensions)**: Quick de-escalation possible but insurance/traffic lag. Suggests 1-3 months partial, 6+ full.
5. **Broader post-war recoveries (e.g., post-2003 Iraq)**: Infrastructure/insurance lag years.

**Base-rate prior** (pre-case evidence): Low short-term (military pauses common but commercial lags). ~5-15% by 1 month; 20-40% by 3 months; 50-70% by 6-12 months; higher at 18 months but skepticism on full proxy/insurance reset.<grok:render card_id="8c2ead" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">75</argument></grok:render>

### Evidence Ledger (selected key items)
- **Low traffic (20-34 vessels/day)**: Vessel trackers/shipping reports; strongly against; high confidence, confirmed.<grok:render card_id="e9b45b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">64</argument></grok:render>
- **Recent strikes/ship attacks & ceasefire "over"**: US/Iranian statements, media; against; high confidence, confirmed but claims disputed on scale.<grok:render card_id="d5dcff" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">20</argument></grok:render>
- **Elevated insurance premiums**: Broker/insurer reports; against; high confidence.
- **Partial transits with US coordination**: CENTCOM; toward limited recovery; confirmed but insufficient for normality.
- **Talks ongoing**: Diplomatic reporting; weakly toward; medium confidence, fragile history.
- **Oil price volatility/supply concerns**: Market data; against full normality.

### Key Drivers
**Toward Normalization**: US military superiority/can deter closure; economic incentives for all (Gulf exporters, Asia importers, Iran); diplomatic channels active; historical precedent for eventual de-escalation.<grok:render card_id="d4252e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">75</argument></grok:render>

**Against (ranked)**: 
1. Iran's asymmetric leverage (mines, proxies, small boats, missiles) and incentive to retain Hormuz influence.
2. Deep mistrust/post-Khamenei hardline IRGC role.
3. Insurer/shipper risk aversion (memory of attacks persists).
4. Proxy networks and potential for sparks.
5. US domestic/political dynamics.

### Decomposed Sub-Forecasts (approximate by horizon)
- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher (40-70% at 3-6mo) as costly.
- Sustained safe commercial transit: Lower (lags military).
- Insurance normalization: Slowest gating factor.
- Export recovery: 3-6mo partial possible if secure.
- Proxy restraint/force drawdown/no escalation: Medium, load-bearing assumptions on restraint.

### Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon
**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero in active flare-up references.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Recent strikes/closure declarations dominate.  
• Core rationale: Ongoing tit-for-tat; traffic minimal.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate de-escalation absent.  
• What would raise: Rapid truce + US escorts.  
• What would lower: Further ship attacks.  
• Confidence: Medium

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from reference classes.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Fragile talks but history of collapse.  
• Core rationale: Insurance/shipper caution persists even post-pause.  
• Main gating factor: Verifiable security for transits.  
• What would raise: Successful mediation + no incidents.  
• What would lower: Renewed major strikes.  
• Confidence: Medium

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: Partial recoveries in Gulf cases.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Damage + mistrust slow commercial return.<grok:render card_id="643ded" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">76</argument></grok:render>  
• Core rationale: Possible military pause but full domains lag.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained insurance/transit confidence.  
• What would raise: Durable agreement + demining.  
• What would lower: Proxy flare or nuclear issue.  
• Confidence: Medium

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: Many references show substantial recovery.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Incentives align but Iran leverage remains.  
• Core rationale: Production/export ramp possible; commercial lags addressed if no escalation.  
• Main gating factor: Proxy restraint + insurer repricing.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive deal + US/Gulf security guarantees.  
• What would lower: Regime change attempts or major incident.  
• Confidence: Medium

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: Longer horizons favor stabilization.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Structural changes (new equilibrium) but fatigue likely.  
• Core rationale: Economic costs high for all; partial normalization probable.  
• Main gating factor: Enduring force posture shift.  
• What would raise: Successful final nuclear/Strait deal.  
• What would lower: Renewed war or proxy war escalation.  
• Confidence: Medium-Low (long horizon uncertainty)

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: Most conflicts eventually stabilize commercially.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Persistent Iranian capabilities cap full return.  
• Core rationale: Definition demanding; new "equilibrium" with elevated baseline risk likely.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of triggers + rebuilt confidence.  
• What would raise: Regional détente.  
• What would lower: Major new crisis.  
• Confidence: Low (third-order effects dominate)

**Synthesis**: Sub-components are not independent; security/transit/insurance are gating. Military pauses enable but do not guarantee commercial normalization (evident in references). Probabilities rise with time but plateau due to load-bearing assumptions on restraint.<grok:render card_id="a5a422" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">22</argument></grok:render>

**Most Likely Path**: Volatile "no war, no peace" with intermittent incidents, partial traffic (~50-70% normal by 6mo if paused), elevated insurance/risk premium persisting. Slow export ramp; new status quo with Iranian influence.

**Faster Normalization Case**: Durable US-brokered deal with security guarantees, demining, proxy stand-down; shippers/insurers return quickly (strong economic push). Strongest evidence: Rapid traffic rebound post-MoU attempts.
