1. **Iran-Iraq Tanker War (1980s)**: Relevant for persistent low-level maritime harassment in Hormuz/Gulf over years; shipping adapted with escorts/insurance spikes but full normalization tied to broader war end (1988 ceasefire). Timeline for reduced attacks: months-years post-major de-escalation; commercial flows slow to recover fully. Breaks down: modern precision weapons, higher economic stakes, US direct involvement. Suggests 6-18+ months for functional normality.<grok:render card_id="ed6920" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">91</argument></grok:render>

2. **Red Sea/Houthi Crisis (2023-ongoing into 2026)**: Relevant for proxy-driven shipping deterrence, insurance spikes, rerouting. Traffic recovered slowly even with naval presence; full normalization elusive without political resolution. Suggests partial recovery in 3-6 months under protection, full in 6-12+ with diplomacy.

3. **Post-Gulf War 1991 or Iraq War 2003 stabilization phases**: Major conflict ends → force drawdown and shipping/insurance recovery in weeks-months for direct threats, but commercial confidence lags (insurance, buyer behavior) 3-12 months.

4. **Shorter crises (e.g., 2019-2020 tanker attacks, 2024-25 escalations)**: Quick de-escalation possible but repeated flares; commercial normalization lagged insurance/escort needs by 1-3 months.

**Base-rate prior** (before case-specifics): Low for short horizons (near-zero at 1 week/1 month due to inertia); rises gradually: ~10-20% at 3 months, 40-60% at 6-12 months, 60-80% at 18 months. Chokepoint recoveries are sticky due to second-order effects (insurer caution, rerouting habits, political leverage).<grok:render card_id="222923" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">81</argument></grok:render>

### Evidence Ledger (selected high-impact items)

- **Recent clashes (May 4-5 attacks on vessels/UAE, US responses)**: Primary reporting (CENTCOM, UAE, ISW); strongly against near-term normalization. High confidence, confirmed.<grok:render card_id="293fca" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>
- **Dual blockades + paused Project Freedom but ongoing negotiations**: Official statements (Trump, Iranian officials); mixed but leans against (leverage retained). Confirmed but intent inferred.<grok:render card_id="3c9478" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render>
- **Shipping/insurance disruption (premiums 4-20x, traffic trickle, stranded vessels)**: Industry reports (Lloyd’s, brokers); strongly against. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="f816c6" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">36</argument></grok:render>
- **Oil export cuts, Gulf production adjustments**: Market/energy data; against full recovery. Confirmed.
- **Proxy restraint variable but recent UAE/Oman strikes**: Against. Confirmed in part.
- **Diplomatic progress claims vs. maximalist demands**: Disputed/inferred; thin evidence base for breakthrough.

### Key Drivers Toward Normalization
- US/Iranian incentives for deal (economic pain on both; Trump pause signals flexibility; China/Pakistan mediation).
- US naval superiority for escorted transits if pursued.
- Gulf alternatives (pipelines) and global spare capacity buffering some flows.

### Key Drivers Against Normalization (ranked high impact)
1. **Iran’s leverage strategy** (Hormuz control for concessions on nuclear/sanctions) — core gating.
2. **Fragile ceasefire + recent flares** (trust deficit; easy re-escalation).
3. **Commercial inertia** (insurance, shipper caution, rerouting entrenchment).
4. **Proxy/force posture risks** and political maximalism.
5. **Second-order cascades** (buyer shifts to US/other sources, insurer risk aversion).

### Decomposed Sub-Forecasts (approximate by horizon)
- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher (30-70% by 3-6mo) if diplomacy holds.
- Sustained safe commercial transit: Lower (gated by insurance/attacks).
- Insurance normalization: Lags (slow due to data requirements).
- Export recovery: Medium, but partial reroutes possible.
- Proxy restraint/no new triggers: Variable, ~40-60% medium term.
Gating: Insurance + sustained zero incidents + diplomatic Hormuz agreement.

### Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero from historical chokepoint crises.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Sharp downward (recent clashes, active dual blockades).  
• Core rationale: Immediate kinetic risks and paused-but-unresolved escorts preclude multi-domain normality.  
• Main gating factor: Any new incident resets.  
• What would raise materially: Immediate verifiable truce + safe multi-vessel transit.  
• What would lower materially: Escalation in Gulf.  
• Confidence in this estimate: High

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from Tanker War/Red Sea analogs.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Downward (negotiations fragile, insurance sticky).  
• Core rationale: Time too short for commercial/insurance recovery even with ceasefire hold.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained no-attacks + initial insurance repricing.  
• What would raise materially: Major diplomatic breakthrough + successful large-scale escorted flows.  
• What would lower materially: Renewed strikes.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium-High

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~20-30% from references.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Moderate upward if talks advance, but recent events weigh.  
• Core rationale: Possible partial military de-escalation; commercial lags (insurance needs incident-free data).  
• Main gating factor: Insurance availability + export volumes.  
• What would raise materially: Durable Hormuz agreement + premium drops.  
• What would lower materially: Proxy flare or negotiation collapse.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: 40-60%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward on attrition incentives.  
• Core rationale: Enough time for drawdown and partial commercial return if diplomacy succeeds; second-order effects still bind.  
• Main gating factor: Force posture + market confidence.  
• What would raise materially: Verified drawdown + normalized premiums/transits.  
• What would lower materially: Renewed leadership/nuclear trigger.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: 60%+.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward (longer horizon allows adaptation).  
• Core rationale: Historical recoveries occur within a year post-major phase; load-bearing assumptions are sustained diplomacy and no regime-change push.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of escalation triggers.  
• What would raise materially: Comprehensive deal.  
• What would lower materially: Major new proxy war or strikes.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: High-end reference.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Capped due to enduring Iran leverage tactics and proxy risks.  
• Core rationale: Most cases stabilize by then, but definition is demanding (full commercial/insurance). Evidence supports if war phase ends.  
• Main gating factor: Broader regional/political settlement.  
• What would raise materially: Regime stabilization or major concessions.  
• What would lower materially: Persistent hybrid conflict.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium (long-horizon uncertainty)

**Synthesis**: Sub-components combined via conjunction (insurance/transit as strongest gates; military easier). Not mechanical average—military de-escalation necessary but insufficient without commercial signals. Probabilities rise with time but plateau below 90% due to recurrence risk.<grok:render card_id="42e566" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">37</argument></grok:render>

**Most Likely Path**: Fragile extended truce with intermittent low-level incidents; gradual escorted/partial transits; slow insurance easing by 6-12mo; partial export recovery via alternatives; full multi-domain normality by 12-18mo if nuclear/Hormuz talks yield limited deal.

**Faster Normalization Case** (strongest): Quick US-Iran pragmatic agreement (e.g., sanctions relief for Hormuz access rules); US backstop insurance transitions smoothly; Gulf states stabilize; oil markets reward with lower volatility. Raises all horizons +15-25pts.

**Prolonged Instability Case** (strongest): Iran doubles down on leverage/attacks; proxies activated; negotiations fail over maximalism; insurers remain cautious; rerouting entrenches. Lowers short/medium horizons sharply; 18mo ~50%.

**Red-Team Critique**: I may overestimate normalization speed by underweighting commercial hysteresis (shippers/insurers need prolonged proof) and Iranian domestic incentives to prolong leverage. Conversely, may underestimate US resolve/escalation dominance forcing quicker Iranian concessions. Load-bearing: Assumption of mutual economic pain driving deal (could be asymmetric). Evidence base thin on private negotiations.

**Critical Signals to Monitor**: Successful multi-vessel unescorted transits; war-risk premium trends (Lloyd’s/JWC updates); oil export volume data (Vortexa/Kpler); official statements on Hormuz “management”; proxy attack frequency; US drawdown signals.

**Final Summary Table** (Probabilities %)

| Horizon   | Probability | Key Gate          |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 Week    | 5           | No new clashes    |
| 1 Month   | 15          | Initial de-escalation |
| 3 Months  | 35          | Insurance easing  |
| 6 Months  | 55          | Transit recovery  |
| 1 Year    | 70          | Sustained flows   |
| 18 Months | 80          | Full confidence   |

This forecast prioritizes calibration over narrative; updates warranted on primary indicators.

title: Superforecast: Iran War Normalization Probabilities
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, observable, multi-domain):

Functional normality means all these must hold simultaneously for a sustained period (at least 2–4 weeks without reversal):

- **Direct military activity**: No strikes, exchanges of fire, or attacks by US/Israel/Iran or their forces in/near the Gulf (including Hormuz) or against Gulf state targets.
- **Proxy activity**: No significant Houthi/Hezbollah/PMF/IRGC-QF attacks on shipping, ports, or energy infrastructure traceable to Iranian direction.
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: Safe commercial transit without routine escorts, attacks, mines, or credible threats; AIS/vessel tracking shows consistent traffic.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Vessel traffic and tanker/LNG carrier movements return to ≥70–80% of pre-Feb 2026 baselines (~3,000 vessels/month pre-war).
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Private market premiums normalize to low-single-digit multiples of pre-war levels (e.g., <1% of hull value per transit vs. current 1–5%+ or cancellations); no widespread government backstops or notices of cancellation required.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Persian Gulf producers (Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Iraq, Kuwait, Iran) export at or near pre-war volumes without major storage buildup or forced rerouting; no prolonged halts.
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI and JKM/TTF benchmarks stabilize without war-premium spikes (>20–30% volatility attributable to Gulf risk); no emergency SPR releases or rerouting dominating flows.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/UK/coalition drawdown from heightened escort/blockade posture; Iranian naval/IRGC forces not actively contesting transit; no dual blockades.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No nuclear breakthroughs, leadership changes sparking instability, or proxy surges; sustained diplomatic track (e.g., extended ceasefire with enforcement).

A temporary pause, lower prices from demand destruction, or partial escorted transits do **not** qualify. Normality requires commercial confidence driving insurer and shipper behavior without military crutches.<grok:render card_id="1e5952" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="ec8b39" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">17</argument></grok:render>

**Current Situation Snapshot (as of May 5, 2026)**: War began Feb 28, 2026 (US/Israel strikes on Iran, assassination of Khamenei). Ceasefire ~April 8 (fragile, extended). Recent May 4–5 clashes: Iran attacks on UAE (Fujairah), attempted interference in Hormuz; US sinks Iranian boats, escorts vessels under “Project Freedom.” Dual blockade persists. Shipping traffic near zero for months; insurance canceled/repriced dramatically higher. Gulf exports severely curtailed (e.g., Kuwait zero crude exports in April). Oil ~$100+/bbl with volatility. Situation is active brinkmanship, not post-conflict.<grok:render card_id="3116c2" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="30ff1e" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="79d594" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">13</argument></grok:render>

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**:

1. **Tanker War (1980s Iran-Iraq)**: Relevant—direct Hormuz threats, attacks on shipping, US escorts (Earnest Will). Normalization took years; escorts needed for sustained periods. Breaks down: No full regime change or nuclear element; lower proxy density today. Suggests 6–24+ months for commercial normality.<grok:render card_id="a54e43" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">59</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="c81bed" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">60</argument></grok:render>

2. **1991 Gulf War aftermath (Kuwait/Iraq damage)**: Oil infrastructure recovery 3–12+ months for meaningful exports; full pre-war years. Relevant for export continuity. Breaks down: No ongoing naval chokepoint contest today. Suggests months for exports.<grok:render card_id="015e6f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">81</argument></grok:render>

3. **Red Sea/Houthi crisis (2023–)**: Persistent low-level disruption; rerouting common, insurance elevated for years. Partial recovery slow despite coalitions. Suggests prolonged insurance/shipping caution even post-pause.<grok:render card_id="382990" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">58</argument></grok:render>

4. **Other chokepoint disruptions** (e.g., Suez closures, past Gulf tensions): Commercial traffic rebounds in weeks–months with security, but insurance lags.

**Base-rate prior** (before case evidence): ~5–15% by 1 month; 20–40% by 3 months; 40–60% by 6 months; 60–75% by 1 year; 70–85% by 18 months. Long horizons higher due to historical pressure for energy flows, but demanding definition pulls down short/medium terms.

**Evidence Ledger** (selected key items):

- Recent Hormuz clashes (May 4–5), US escorts, Iranian threats/attacks on UAE: Confirmed via multiple sources (Al Jazeera, CNN, ISW, CENTCOM). Strongly against normalization. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="cc289f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="5adb89" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">13</argument></grok:render>
- Shipping traffic near zero; insurers canceled/repriced (1–5%+ premiums): Confirmed. Strongly against. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="498207" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>
- Ceasefire fragile, tested; dual blockade: Confirmed. Against. Medium-high confidence.
- Limited successful escorted transits (e.g., 2 US-flagged May 4): Confirmed but minimal. Mildly toward. High confidence.
- Gulf export halts (Kuwait zero, Qatar LNG disrupted): Confirmed. Against. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="c41d20" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">79</argument></grok:render>
- US reinsurance/government efforts: Confirmed but insufficient for full private market return. Mildly toward.

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked):
1. Massive economic pressure on all sides (global energy prices, Asian/European buyers).
2. US military superiority in escorts/minesweeping.
3. Iranian degradation (navy, missiles) limiting sustained closure.
4. Diplomatic tracks (Trump statements, proposals).

**Key Drivers Against Normalization** (ranked higher overall):
1. Fragile ceasefire + recent clashes; Iranian incentives to use asymmetric tools (proxies, mines, tolls).
2. Insurance market caution—actuarial memory of attacks (persistent high premiums).
3. Proxy activation risk and escalation triggers (nuclear remnants, leadership instability).
4. Force posture inertia (US escorts needed long-term).
5. Second-order: Buyer/shipper risk aversion cascades to low traffic even if some transits succeed.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (approximate by horizon; gating noted):
- Major reduction in direct strikes: Higher (e.g., 40% at 1 mo, 70% at 3 mo) due to costs.
- Sustained safe commercial transit: Lower (insurance/attacks gate).
- Insurance normalization: Very low short-term; lags heavily.
- Export recovery: Medium; physical restart possible but security/insurance gates.
- Proxy restraint: Low-medium.
- No new escalation: Challenging at short horizons.

**Synthesis to Main Forecast**: Insurance, commercial behavior, and sustained security (without constant military presence) are primary gating factors. Military pauses enable partial transits but not normality. Short horizons dominated by recent clashes; medium by fragile dynamics; longer by structural pressures for recovery. Probabilities rise but plateau due to definition demanding full commercial confidence.<grok:render card_id="4986a1" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">86</argument></grok:render>

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**:

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero from active clashes reference.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Strong downward (May 4–5 fighting).  
• Core rationale: Immediate kinetic activity precludes any domain of normality.  
• Main gating factor: Cessation of direct/proxy fire.  
• What would raise: Rapid de-escalation + Trump/Iran statements.  
• What would lower: Further sinkings/attacks.  
• Confidence: High

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from Tanker War/Red Sea.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Downward (fragile truce testing).  
• Core rationale: Partial escorts possible but insurance/traffic/exports lag; recent violence resets.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained pause + initial insurance repricing.  
• What would raise: Successful multi-vessel transits without incident.  
• What would lower: Ceasefire collapse.  
• Confidence: Medium

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~30% from references.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Mild upward if pause holds.  
• Core rationale: Time for some recovery/export ramps, but insurance and proxies likely persist.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance normalization and proxy restraint.  
• What would raise: Major diplomatic breakthrough + US drawdown.  
• What would lower: Renewed strikes or proxy surge.  
• Confidence: Medium

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~50%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Balanced.  
• Core rationale: Enough time for infrastructure restart and market adaptation, but demanding definition requires commercial confidence beyond escorts.<grok:render card_id="efcb16" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">86</argument></grok:render>  
• Main gating factor: Full private insurance return + traffic volumes.  
• What would raise: Stable exports + volatility drop.  
• What would lower: Persistent low-level threats.  
• Confidence: Medium

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~65–70%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward (historical pressure).  
• Core rationale: Strong incentives align; degradation limits Iran; references show eventual stabilization.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of new triggers + force posture normalization.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive deal.  
• What would lower: Regime instability or proxy war.  
• Confidence: Medium

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: High.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward.  
• Core rationale: Long horizon favors recovery despite setbacks; definition still demanding but evidence supports high likelihood under sustained pressure. Not 90%+ due to structural proxy risks.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained multi-domain stability.  
• What would raise: Broader regional détente.  
• What would lower: Major new escalation.  
• Confidence: Medium

**Most Likely Path**: Fragile extended ceasefire with intermittent low-level incidents and escorted transits. Gradual export recovery over months, insurance lagging 3–9 months, reaching partial normality by 6–12 months if no major breach. Volatility persists.

**Faster Normalization Case** (strongest): Quick US-Iran understanding on Hormuz (e.g., no tolls, limited Iranian presence), successful large-scale escorted convoys without losses, government reinsurance bridging to private markets, proxy restraint. Could accelerate 3–6 month probabilities +20–30 pts.

**Prolonged Instability Case** (strongest): Ceasefire collapses into tit-for-tat (mines, proxies, strikes), insurance market freezes long-term, Iranian asymmetric campaign sustains fear, buyer rerouting entrenches. Delays normality by 12+ months; lowers all horizons 20–40 pts.

**Red-Team Critique**: I may overestimate normalization speed by underweighting insurer risk aversion (actuarial conservatism post-attacks) and proxy durability. Recent clashes suggest higher near-term volatility than modeled. Conversely, may underestimate US leverage and global economic forcing function toward compromise. Load-bearing assumptions: Ceasefire holds at baseline; Iranian capacity remains degraded.

**Critical Signals to Monitor**:
- Successful unescorted/large-scale transits.
- War-risk premium trends and cancellation notices.
- AIS traffic volumes + export data (tanker trackers).
- Official statements on ceasefire status (Trump, Iranian officials).
- Proxy attacks (Houthi, etc.) and Gulf state responses.
- Oil/LNG price volatility and SPR actions.

**Final Summary Table** (Probabilities):

- 1 Week: 5%
- 1 Month: 15%
- 3 Months: 35%
- 6 Months: 55%
- 1 Year: 70%
- 18 Months: 80%

This forecast balances reference classes with current thin but consistent evidence of fragility. Updates will follow major incidents or diplomatic shifts.

title: Gulf normality forecast updated
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, observable, multi-domain):<grok:render card_id="d8c246" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="578d1f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">1</argument></grok:render>

Functional normality means **all** of the following sustained for at least 30 consecutive days without major reversal:
- **Direct military activity**: No strikes/exchanges between US/Israel and Iran (or their forces); IRGC/USN/CENTCOM posture reverts toward pre-Feb 2026 levels.
- **Proxy activity**: No significant new Houthi/Hezbollah/PMF attacks tied to the Iran theater; restraint holds.
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: No attacks, mining, or credible threats; US “Project Freedom” escorts unnecessary; AIS/transit data shows routine safe passage.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Vessel traffic through Hormuz returns to ≥80% of 2025 pre-war baseline (~20-21 million bpd oil equivalent + LNG).
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums fall to low single-digit add-ons (not 10x+ war rates); underwriters remove “war zone” exclusions or high deductibles.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Iranian, Saudi, UAE, Iraqi, Qatari exports flow at near-capacity without forced curtailments; no major stranded tankers or force majeure declarations.
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent/WTI within ~15% of pre-war trends with normal backwardation/contango; no sustained >$20-30/bbl risk premium from Gulf disruption.
- **Force posture of major actors**: USN drawdown from blockade/escort levels; Iranian naval/IRGC forces not on high alert for closure; Gulf states resume normal operations.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No nuclear breakout moves, leadership decapitation follow-ons, or proxy surges; credible diplomatic track (e.g., Hormuz guarantees + sanctions relief path) active.

A temporary pause, lowered (but still elevated) oil prices, or battlefield lull does **not** qualify. Commercial/insurance behavior is the decisive lagging indicator.<grok:render card_id="31ff1f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">16</argument></grok:render>

### Current Situation Snapshot (as of ~May 4, 2026)
Fragile ceasefire since ~April 8 holds for direct US-Iran strikes, but dual blockades persist: US naval blockade of Iranian ports + Iranian restrictions/tolls/threats in Hormuz. Traffic at ~5% of normal. US launching “Project Freedom” escorts. Negotiations stalled (Trump rejected latest Iranian proposal). Iran reconstituting capabilities; oil exports curtailed; high market volatility and insurance rates. Evidence base is current but thin on proprietary shipping/insurance data.<grok:render card_id="ad8e8a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="09bda6" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">2</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="2f1287" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">5</argument></grok:render>

### Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior
Relevant classes (outside view first):

1. **1980s Tanker War (Iran-Iraq)**: Highly relevant—attacks on shipping in same waters, US escort operations (Earnest Will), mines/speedboats. Disruption lasted years with intermittent attacks; full normalization post-1988 ceasefire took months-years for insurance/traffic confidence. Suggests 6-18+ months for commercial return even after formal end.<grok:render card_id="b80554" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">60</argument></grok:render>

2. **1991 Gulf War oil disruptions/spill**: Short intense phase; shipping recovered relatively quickly post-ceasefire (weeks-months) once mines cleared and threats gone, aided by coalition victory. Less relevant due to decisive outcome vs. current stalemate.<grok:render card_id="d8e00f" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">81</argument></grok:render>

3. **Red Sea/Houthi crisis (2023-2025/26)**: Proxy-driven attacks; rerouting persisted long after peaks; partial recovery slow (many lines hesitant even post-pauses). Months to years for full confidence. Good analog for asymmetric threats/insurance lag.<grok:render card_id="195b02" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">92</argument></grok:render>

4. **Suez closures (1956, 1967-75)**: Full closures; 1967-75 took 8 years due to war/ politics. Extreme but shows chokepoint psychology lingers.<grok:render card_id="1cf609" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">72</argument></grok:render>

5. **Shorter disruptions** (e.g., Ever Given 2021): Days/weeks for physical fix, but supply chain ripple months. Not war-scale.

**Base-rate prior** (pre-case evidence): Low short-term; gradual long-term. ~5-15% by 1-3 months, 30-50% by 6 months, 60-75% by 1 year, 75-85% by 18 months for functional (commercial-led) normalization. War chokepoints with proxies/dual blockades resolve slowly.

### Evidence Ledger (selected key items)
- **Dual blockade + low traffic (~5% normal)**: Confirmed (satellite/AIS, CENTCOM, shipping reports). Strongly against near-term normality. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="cd1766" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">16</argument></grok:render>
- **Ceasefire holding for direct strikes since Apr 8**: Confirmed. Toward (but insufficient alone). High.
- **Iranian proposals/rejections; stalled talks (nuclear/Hormuz preconditions)**: Reported (WSJ, ISW, Trump statements). Disputed interpretations on sincerity. Mixed, leans against. Medium-high.<grok:render card_id="8736c6" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">2</argument></grok:render>
- **US Project Freedom escorts starting**: Confirmed. Could accelerate but risks clashes. Toward if successful/no escalation. Medium.
- **Iran reconstituting missiles; “still in war situation”**: Reported. Against sustained restraint. Medium.
- **Oil production cuts, stranded tankers (~$5B lost)**: Confirmed. Against export continuity. High.
- **Insurance/war-risk elevated; rerouting**: Inferred from behavior/pricing reports. Strongly against.

### Key Drivers Toward Normalization
- Strong US/Gulf interest in reopening (energy security, revenues).
- Economic pain on Iran (storage limits, revenue loss) pushing for deal.
- Diplomatic track (Pakistan mediation) and Trump leverage.
- Successful escorts without clashes could build confidence rapidly.

### Key Drivers Against (ranked high impact)
1. **Stalemate on core issues** (Hormuz control, nuclear, blockade lift) — gating.
2. **Proxy reconstitution + escalation risk** (IRGC, Hezbollah spillover).
3. **Insurance/shipping risk aversion** — lags military pauses by months (reference classes).
4. **Iranian leverage retention** over strait (tolls, threats).
5. **US domestic/political factors** and force posture maintenance.

### Decomposed Sub-Forecasts (approximate by horizon)
- Major reduction in direct strikes: High short-term (~70% 1mo, 85% 3mo) but reversible.
- Sustained safe commercial transit: Low short (10-20% 1mo), medium 3-6mo (40-60%).
- Insurance normalization: Lagging (20% 3mo, 50% 6mo, 75% 1yr).
- Oil/LNG export recovery: Constrained by above.
- Proxy restraint: Medium, ~50% sustained at 6mo.
- No new escalation trigger: ~60-70% at 6mo, lower long-term due to nuclear/leadership issues.
Gating: Commercial/insurance + diplomatic resolution of blockades.

### Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon
**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero in active chokepoint wars.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Dual blockades + new US operation make rapid commercial shift impossible.  
• Core rationale: Traffic/insurance unchanged; escorts just starting.  
• Main gating factor: Physical/diplomatic breakthrough.  
• Raise materially: Immediate full reopening agreement.  
• Lower materially: Clash during escorts.  
• Confidence: High

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from Tanker War/Red Sea analogs.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Fragile ceasefire but stalled talks + reconstitution.  
• Core rationale: Project Freedom may free some ships but not normalize behavior.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance/shipping confidence.  
• Raise materially: Major diplomatic concession (e.g., mutual blockade lift).  
• Lower materially: Renewed strikes or attack on escorted vessel.  
• Confidence: Medium-High

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: Partial stabilization post-pause in analogs ~20-40%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Economic pressure builds; escorts test waters.  
• Core rationale: Possible partial traffic recovery if no clashes, but full multi-domain lag.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained transit without incidents.  
• Raise materially: Credible long-term Hormuz guarantee + sanctions path.  
• Lower materially: Proxy surge or nuclear move.  
• Confidence: Medium

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: Many chokepoint cases see material progress.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Prolonged pain likely forces compromise, but proxies linger.  
• Core rationale: Insurance normalizes slowly; exports recover if security holds.  
• Main gating factor: Diplomatic resolution of core disputes.  
• Raise materially: Formal agreement + drawdowns.  
• Lower materially: Regime instability or major violation.  
• Confidence: Medium

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: Post-major conflict stabilization often 60-80%.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: High incentives for both sides; but history of Iranian hedging.  
• Core rationale: Commercial adaptation + fatigue drive recovery, though not pre-war perfect.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of new triggers + force posture shifts.  
• Raise materially: Broader regional deals (e.g., Saudi-Iran).  
• Lower materially: Renewed direct conflict.  
• Confidence: Medium

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: Long-horizon reference classes favor eventual return.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Even stalled cases resolve or adapt; definition remains demanding (full commercial/insurance).  
• Core rationale: Sustained pressure + global interest; but proxies/nuclear could prevent “functional.”  
• Main gating factor: Enduring diplomatic framework.  
• Raise materially: Verified de-escalation + traffic data.  
• Lower materially: Persistent hybrid threats or breakout.  
• Confidence: Medium (long-horizon uncertainty)

**Synthesis**: Sub-components combined qualitatively—military pause is necessary but insufficient; commercial/insurance are decisive gates (lagging). Not mechanical average; weighted toward slower commercial normalization per references. Probabilities rise with time but capped by demanding definition and stalemate risks.<grok:render card_id="6a605b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">18</argument></grok:render>

### Most Likely Path
Prolonged coercive negotiations with intermittent escort incidents; partial traffic recovery by 3-6 months if no major clash; fuller (but imperfect) normalization by 12-18 months via messy compromise on Hormuz guarantees + limited sanctions relief. Persistent elevated risk premium.

### Faster Normalization Case (~20-30% odds overall)
Quick mutual concessions (Iran lifts restrictions for blockade end + limited nuclear freeze); successful escorts build confidence fast; Gulf states mediate. Traffic/insurance rebound by 3 months. Strongest evidence: Iranian storage crisis forcing deal.

### Prolonged Instability Case
Stalemate persists; proxies activated; minor clashes during escorts; insurance stays punitive. Traffic <50% normal for 12+ months. Strongest evidence: Iranian “never pre-war” statements + reconstitution.

### Red-Team Critique
I may overestimate normalization speed if US escalates or Iran miscalculates (underweighting IRGC hardliners). Or underestimate if economic pain + Trump leverage force faster deal than analogs suggest (shipping adapts quicker with escorts). Load-bearing: Assumption ceasefire holds short-term and diplomacy continues; evidence thin on exact insurance thresholds. Wrong if major new strike or nuclear escalation.

### Critical Signals to Monitor
- Traffic/AIS volumes + successful escorted transits without incident.
- Insurance premium changes (Lloyd’s/Broker reports).
- Iranian oil storage/exports + statements on Hormuz “rights.”
- US/Iran proposal details and Trump reactions.
- Proxy incidents (Houthi/Hezbollah).
- Satellite/military posture shifts.

### Final Summary Table
Horizon | Prob | Key Gate  
---|---|---  
1 Week | 5% | Immediate breakthrough (unlikely)  
1 Month | 15% | Early escort success  
3 Months | 35% | Partial transit + no clashes  
6 Months | 55% | Diplomatic progress  
1 Year | 70% | Commercial confidence  
18 Months | 80% | Sustained framework

This is calibrated, evidence-grounded, and stresses the military-commercial gap. Updates warranted on new primary reporting.

title: Iran War: Gulf Normalization at 5%
message:
**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”** (measurable, observable, multi-domain):

Functional normality means:
- **Direct military activity**: No kinetic strikes (missiles, drones, naval clashes) between Iran/US/Israel or their forces in/near the Gulf for ≥30 consecutive days.
- **Proxy activity**: Significant restraint (≥70% reduction from peak) by Hezbollah, Houthis, PMF, etc., with no major Gulf-targeted attacks.
- **Shipping security in Strait of Hormuz/nearby waters**: Sustained safe commercial transit (no attacks/mining on commercial vessels); US/Iran blockades lifted or ineffective; routine naval escorts unnecessary.
- **Commercial transit levels**: Daily transits ≥70-80% of pre-war baseline (~100-140 vessels/day); backlog of stranded ships (~800-2,000) largely cleared.
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums return to low single-digit multiples of pre-war (e.g., <1% hull value vs. current 1-5%+ or cancellations); full private market coverage available without government backstops.
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Gulf exports (Saudi, UAE, Iraq, Qatar, etc.) at ≥85% pre-war levels; Iranian exports normalized without selective tolls/blockades; no widespread force majeure.
- **Energy market stress/volatility**: Brent/WTI volatility index normalized (no sustained >$100/bbl spikes or rationing); Asian/European buyers resuming standard contracts.
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/Coalition drawdown from heightened alert; Iran/IRGC not posturing for closure; Gulf states resuming routine operations.
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No unresolved nuclear/missile issues, leadership assassinations, or proxy flare-ups driving immediate risk premia.

A pause or partial reopening does not qualify; commercial/insurance behavior must confirm de-risking.<grok:render card_id="9c6db0" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="15bae7" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render>

**Current Situation Snapshot (as of ~May 3, 2026)**: War began Feb 28 with US/Israeli strikes (assassination of Ali Khamenei, damage to Iranian capabilities). Fragile ceasefire since ~April 8 (US-Iran) and mid-April (Israel-Hezbollah). Dual blockade persists: Iran controls/selectively tolls Hormuz traffic; US blockades Iranian ports. Traffic ~5-10% normal (few to ~14 vessels/day, many selective/IRGC-linked). Hundreds/thousands of ships stranded. Insurance largely unavailable or prohibitive. Oil prices elevated/volatility high. Negotiations stalled (Iran's latest 14-point proposal rejected by Trump). Iran reconstituting capabilities; proxies active in Lebanon. Evidence base: mix of confirmed (traffic data, CENTCOM statements) and disputed claims (Iranian "new management," US effectiveness).<grok:render card_id="43d4bb" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="3e91fe" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="38f3a8" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">79</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="bef69a" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">80</argument></grok:render>

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**:
1. **1980s Tanker War (Iran-Iraq)**: Relevant for proxy/mining/insurance-driven disruptions in same geography. Normalization took years of escorts (US Operation Earnest Will 1987+); full commercial return post-1988 ceasefire gradual (months-years for insurance/routines). Breaks down: lower tech, no US direct war on Iran. Suggests 6-18+ months for functional recovery.<grok:render card_id="1b35ad" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">47</argument></grok:render>
2. **1990-91 Gulf War (Iraq invasion/Kuwait liberation)**: Oil infrastructure damage + disruption. Exports halted; Kuwait recovery 1-2+ years for meaningful exports, 5-7 for full. Shipping normalized faster post-liberation but with lingering risks. Relevant for chokepoint/oil shock. Breaks down: conventional occupation vs. current hybrid/blockade. Suggests 3-12 months partial, longer full.<grok:render card_id="7fe673" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">69</argument></grok:render>
3. **Red Sea/Houthi crisis (2023-25+)**: Proxy attacks drove rerouting, high insurance. Partial recovery slow (months post-de-escalation attempts); full normalization 12-24+ months even after pauses due to lingering risk. Highly relevant for insurance/shipping behavior. Suggests protracted commercial lag.<grok:render card_id="27c471" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">58</argument></grok:render>
4. **Other chokepoint crises** (e.g., Suez 2021, minor Gulf incidents): Days-weeks for physical, but risk premia linger weeks-months.

**Base-rate prior** (pre-case adjustment): Very low short-term; ~10-25% by 3mo, 40-60% by 6-12mo, 60-80% by 18mo for functional (not full pre-war) normality. Commercial/insurance lags battlefield by 3-12+ months.<grok:render card_id="e45814" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render>

**Evidence Ledger** (summary table format):

- Confirmed high-impact: Traffic <10% normal, dual blockade, insurance cancellations/high premia, ceasefire holding but strained (CENTCOM, satellite/tracking, insurers). Negative. High confidence.<grok:render card_id="510b02" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">80</argument></grok:render>
- Confirmed: Iran reconstituting missiles, charging tolls/selective passage; US turning ships. Negative. High.<grok:render card_id="fad106" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">11</argument></grok:render>
- Disputed/inferred: Full Iranian "victory"/control claims vs. US "effective" blockade; proposal rejections. Mixed-negative. Medium.
- Positive: No major direct strikes since April; some selective transits; diplomatic channels open. Weak positive. Medium.

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked):
1. Strong economic incentives (Gulf states, Asia buyers, global markets) for de-escalation.
2. US/Israeli military degradation of Iranian capabilities limiting sustained closure.
3. Diplomatic channels (Pakistan, China mediation).

**Key Drivers Against** (dominant):
1. Core disputes (nuclear, Hormuz control, US presence, sanctions) unresolved; Iran views strait as leverage.<grok:render card_id="5e036b" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">17</argument></grok:render>
2. Proxy risks and reconstitution.
3. Insurance/shipping hysteresis: behavior lags security by months.
4. Dual blockade and toll/seizure risks.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (by horizon, approximate % for key components):
- Major reduction direct strikes: High short-term (ceasefire), but resumption risk ~40-60% medium-term.
- Safe sustained transit: Very low short (blockades/tolls), rising slowly.
- Insurance normalization: Lagging (6-12+ mo).
- Export recovery: Gated by transit/insurance.
- Proxy restraint/no escalation: Medium, volatile.
Gating: Security + commercial confidence.

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**:

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: Near-zero in active/blockade cases.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Ceasefire holding but blockades/tolls active; traffic minimal.  
• Core rationale: No time for commercial shift.  
• Main gating factor: Immediate blockade lift (unlikely).  
• What would raise materially: Sudden full reopening + safe transits.  
• What would lower materially: Incident or proposal collapse.  
• Confidence: Medium (short horizon observable).

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: Low from references.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Negotiations stalled; reconstitution ongoing.  
• Core rationale: Partial talks possible but commercial lag.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance/shipping confidence.  
• What would raise: Major diplomatic breakthrough + US blockade easing.  
• What would lower: Resumption of strikes or proxy escalation.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~20-30% adjusted up slightly for ceasefire resilience.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Degradation of Iranian forces favors pauses, but core issues persist.  
• Core rationale: Possible partial transit increase but full criteria demanding.  
• Main gating factor: Sustained safe passages + premium drops.  
• What would raise: Comprehensive deal including Hormuz guarantees.  
• What would lower: Proxy flare or failed talks.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 55%  
• Base-rate anchor: References suggest 40-60% range.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Economic pressure builds toward compromise, but hysteresis strong.  
• Core rationale: Time for testing routes/insurance return if security holds.  
• Main gating factor: Export flows and market volatility decline.  
• What would raise: Verified drawdowns + multiple incident-free months.  
• What would lower: Renewed closure or major incident.  
• Confidence: Medium-High.

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 70%  
• Base-rate anchor: Upper end of references for partial stabilization.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Long enough for rebuilding/re-routing alternatives; incentives align.  
• Core rationale: Most conflicts see de-risking, but definition demanding.  
• Main gating factor: Full commercial/insurance normalization.  
• What would raise: Durable political settlement.  
• What would lower: Regime change instability or new nuclear crisis.  
• Confidence: Medium.

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: High from historical eventual recovery.  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Skeptical of >80% given load-bearing assumptions on restraint.  
• Core rationale: Enough time for cycles to resolve but proxies/nuclear enduring risks.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of triggers + force posture normalization.  
• What would raise: Regional détente (e.g., Gulf-Iran thaw).  
• What would lower: Escalation spiral.  
• Confidence: Medium (long-horizon uncertainty).<grok:render card_id="38ed13" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">0</argument></grok:render><grok:render card_id="6470cf" card_type="citation_card" type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">42</argument></grok:render>

**Most Likely Path**: Fragile extended ceasefire with managed/low-volume transits, periodic tensions, slow insurance easing by 6-9mo, partial export recovery by 12mo. Not full pre-war; "new normal" with higher baseline risk.

**Faster Normalization Case** (~+20-30% probabilities): Rapid US-Iran deal lifting blockades, Iran concessions on nuclear/strait, successful escorts → commercial rebound in 3-6mo. Strongest evidence: Gulf economic pain + US leverage.

title: Gulf test compliance day 5, transits up to 34.
message:
**Forecast Question**  
Estimate the probability that the Persian Gulf has returned to functional normality following the outbreak of the 2026 Iran War by each horizon: 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 18 months.

**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”**  
“Return to functional normality” is defined operationally and observably across domains as:  
- **Direct military activity**: Zero confirmed US/Israeli strikes on Iranian targets or Iranian missile/drone/naval attacks on Gulf shipping/assets for ≥30 consecutive days.  
- **Proxy activity**: Hezbollah/Houthi/militia attacks on Gulf or related targets at ≤5 incidents per month (verified via UKMTO/CENTCOM reporting).  
- **Shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: Sustained transit with <1 confirmed attack per month and US/coalition naval escort presence at pre-war levels.  
- **Commercial transit levels**: Average daily vessel crossings ≥100 (≥80% of pre-war baseline of ~135–138), sustained for ≥30 days (via AIS/tanker-tracker data).  
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums ≤0.5% of hull value (renewable without special US backstop), full P&I coverage available without force majeure clauses.  
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Gulf exports (Saudi, Qatar, UAE, Kuwait, Iraq) at ≥90% of pre-war volumes (IEA/Kpler data); no force majeure declarations; Iranian exports secondary.  
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent crude volatility index ≤ historical peacetime average (~15–20%); no sustained supply shock premiums.  
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/Israeli/Gulf forces at DEFCON-equivalent 4 or below with partial drawdowns; no heightened alerts or mine-laying.  
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No strikes on Kharg Island oil facilities, Ras Tanura, Ras Laffan, or equivalent for ≥60 days.  

A temporary ceasefire or battlefield pause does not qualify. Lower oil prices alone do not qualify. Commercial normalization must lag military pauses by weeks due to insurer and buyer risk aversion.

**Current Situation Snapshot**  
As of 2 May 2026 (~Day 66 since onset), the US naval blockade remains formally in place with enforcement restricted to passive monitoring. Windward data record 34 transits on 1 May (volumes ~75% below pre-war baseline). Day 5 of the 10-day verification test under the 28 April preliminary understanding reports “compliance sustained with no deviations observed on designated corridor access points” per the joint Omani monitoring team; both sides have reaffirmed commitment to uninterrupted daily reporting through the full window. No new vessel attacks, seizures, or proxy activations reported in the past 240 hours. Ras Laffan force majeure and 3–5 year repair timeline (17% Qatar LNG capacity loss) unchanged. Houthi Bab el-Mandeb signaling non-activated.

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**  
Reference classes (outside-in base rates before case-specific adjustment):  

1. **Iran-Iraq Tanker War (1980–88)**: Relevant for identical chokepoint attacks, insurance spikes, and export halts. Timeline to functional commercial recovery: 6–18+ months post-ceasefire once escorts and premiums aligned. Breaks down because modern coalition naval assets and satellite tracking allow faster threat suppression than in the 1980s. Suggests gradual long-term stabilization only.  

2. **2019–2020 Iranian tanker/Abqaiq attacks**: Relevant for short-duration Hormuz disruptions and temporary premium surges. Recovery: commercial volumes and insurance terms returned to baseline within 1–3 months after de-escalation. Breaks down due to far lower intensity and absence of state-on-state missile exchanges. Suggests modest short-term probabilities if fighting ends abruptly.  

3. **Red Sea Houthi crisis (2023–ongoing as of early 2026)**: Relevant for proxy-driven rerouting, elevated war-risk quotes, and partial export adjustments. Partial normalization: 6–12 months before premiums fell and schedules stabilized. Breaks down because scale was smaller and no direct Iranian state involvement. Suggests commercial recovery trails military calm by months.  

4. **1991 Gulf War**: Relevant for rapid kinetic phase followed by coalition naval clearance. Timeline: 1–3 months to restored transit and insurance norms. Breaks down because current conflict lacks decisive ground component or immediate regime outcome. Suggests faster recovery only under clear military resolution.  

5. **2003 Iraq War opening phase**: Relevant for Gulf-area port and export interruptions during regime-change fighting. Recovery: shipping and volumes normalized in 2–6 months once major combat subsided. Breaks down because Hormuz itself was never closed.  

**Base-rate prior** (timeline-based, pre-evidence):  
- 1 week: ~1%  
- 1 month: ~5%  
- 3 months: ~15–20%  
- 6 months: ~30–40%  
- 1 year: ~50–60%  
- 18 months: ~65–75%  

**Evidence Ledger**  

| Evidence Item | Source Type | Direction of Impact on Normalization | Confidence Level | Confirmed/Disputed/Inferred |
|---------------|-------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| No turn-backs, boardings, or shadowing reported in past 168 hours (enforcement passive monitoring only) | CENTCOM / Reuters 1–2 May | Toward (continued enforcement pause) | High | Confirmed |
| Windward data: 34 transits on 1 May (volumes ~75% below baseline) | Windward Maritime Intelligence Daily (1 May) / Bloomberg 1–2 May | Mildly toward (continued daily uptick) but overall against | High | Confirmed |
| Day 5 verification test reports “compliance sustained with no deviations observed on designated corridor access points” | Joint Omani monitoring team readout / Reuters / Al Jazeera 2 May | Toward (positive multi-day test signal past halfway mark) | High | Confirmed |
| Both sides reaffirm commitment to uninterrupted daily reporting through full 10-day window | US State Department / Iranian Foreign Ministry / Reuters 2 May | Toward (test framework stable) | High | Confirmed |
| No new vessel attacks, seizures, or proxy activations in past 240 hours | UANI / CENTCOM-linked updates 30 Apr–2 May | Toward (extended pause) | High | Confirmed |
| Ras Laffan 17% capacity loss, 3–5 year repairs, QatarEnergy force majeure unchanged | QatarEnergy / Reuters ongoing | Strongly against | High | Confirmed |
| Houthi Bab el-Mandeb signaling unchanged and non-activated | MARAD / Al Jazeera 9 Apr–2 May | Neutral | High | Confirmed |

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked)  
1. Day 5 verification test reports sustained compliance past the halfway point with reaffirmed daily reporting.  
2. Passive enforcement and transit uptick to 34 vessels/day.  
3. 240-hour attack-free period.

**Key Drivers Against Normalization** (ranked)  
1. Blockade formally remains in force.  
2. Transit volumes locked at ~75% below baseline.  
3. Binding Ras Laffan constraints and force majeure.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (by horizon; key gating components)  
- Major reduction in direct strikes: 1 wk ~23%, 1 mo ~36%, 3 mo ~57%, 6 mo ~77%, 1 yr ~94%, 18 mo ~98%.  
- Sustained safe commercial transit (>80% levels): 1 wk ~13%, 1 mo ~18%, 3 mo ~28%, 6 mo ~45%, 1 yr ~65%, 18 mo ~83%.  
- Meaningful insurance normalization: lags transit; 1 wk ~12%, 1 mo ~17%, 3 mo ~26%, 6 mo ~42%, 1 yr ~62%, 18 mo ~79%.  
- Oil/LNG export recovery: gated by terminal restarts + transit; similar lag profile.  
- Proxy restraint + force drawdown + no new triggers: tracks direct-strike reduction but heavily discounted by formal blockade status.

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**  

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 15%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~1%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from multi-day test compliance past halfway and continued enforcement pause.  
• Core rationale: Test momentum now exceeds half the verification window but blockade and volume thresholds still dominate the immediate 7-day window.  
• Main gating factor: Remaining test days or any enforcement reversal.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Consistent compliance through day 7+ or early phased easing.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Test deviation or new interdiction.  
• Confidence in this estimate: High  

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 22%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~5%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from sustained test progress past halfway.  
• Core rationale: Verification process now generating extended data but commercial/insurance lags persist under formal blockade.  
• Main gating factor: Commercial transit volumes.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Full 10-day test completion with positive outcome.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Any test deviation or reversal.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 35%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~15–20%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from repeated test signals past halfway.  
• Core rationale: Verification framework holding steady yet commercial/insurance recovery still trails formal blockade.  
• Main gating factor: 30-day safe-transit threshold.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Verified full implementation of phased measures.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Test collapse or re-escalation.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 54%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~30–40%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward from test momentum.  
• Core rationale: Interval supports capability degradation and partial rebound if kinetic phase subsides.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance quote stabilization.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Iranian internal pressure signals.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Entrenched proxy or blockade campaign.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 73%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~50–60%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward from verification progress.  
• Core rationale: Chokepoint cases historically normalize commercially inside one year post-peak.  
• Main gating factor: Export volume continuity.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Proxy settlement.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Fragmented post-conflict dynamics.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium-High  

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 90%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~65–75%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward; test data reachable.  
• Core rationale: Prolonged maritime conflicts achieve functional recovery; effects dissipate. Operational definition remains demanding because insurance reinstatement, buyer behavior shifts, and physical Ras Laffan repairs impose multi-month lags even after kinetic calm.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of fresh escalation triggers.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Coalition enforcement success.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Persistent militia autonomy.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**Most Likely Path**  
Day 5 verification test confirms sustained compliance and daily reporting continues uninterrupted; transits remain in low double digits (~29–35/day) while blockade stays formally intact but passive. Negotiated pause possible mid-September if full 10-day test completes successfully; commercial volumes and insurance terms follow with 12–16 week lag. **Forecast Question**  
Estimate the probability that the Persian Gulf has returned to functional normality following the outbreak of the 2026 Iran War by each horizon: 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 18 months.

**Operational Definition of “Return to Functional Normality”**  
“Return to functional normality” is defined operationally and observably across domains as:  
- **Direct military activity**: Zero confirmed US/Israeli strikes on Iranian targets or Iranian missile/drone/naval attacks on Gulf shipping/assets for ≥30 consecutive days.  
- **Proxy activity**: Hezbollah/Houthi/militia attacks on Gulf or related targets at ≤5 incidents per month (verified via UKMTO/CENTCOM reporting).  
- **Shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters**: Sustained transit with <1 confirmed attack per month and US/coalition naval escort presence at pre-war levels.  
- **Commercial transit levels**: Average daily vessel crossings ≥100 (≥80% of pre-war baseline of ~135–138), sustained for ≥30 days (via AIS/tanker-tracker data).  
- **War-risk insurance conditions**: Premiums ≤0.5% of hull value (renewable without special US backstop), full P&I coverage available without force majeure clauses.  
- **Oil and LNG export continuity**: Gulf exports (Saudi, Qatar, UAE, Kuwait, Iraq) at ≥90% of pre-war volumes (IEA/Kpler data); no force majeure declarations; Iranian exports secondary.  
- **Energy market stress and volatility**: Brent crude volatility index ≤ historical peacetime average (~15–20%); no sustained supply shock premiums.  
- **Force posture of major actors**: US/Israeli/Gulf forces at DEFCON-equivalent 4 or below with partial drawdowns; no heightened alerts or mine-laying.  
- **Absence of major new escalation triggers**: No strikes on Kharg Island oil facilities, Ras Tanura, Ras Laffan, or equivalent for ≥60 days.  

A temporary ceasefire or battlefield pause does not qualify. Lower oil prices alone do not qualify. Commercial normalization must lag military pauses by weeks due to insurer and buyer risk aversion.

**Current Situation Snapshot**  
As of 10 April 2026 (~Day 44 since onset), Iran’s selective permission-based regime via Larak Island remains in place, yet JMIC/Windward data record 42 vessels transiting on 8 April (seventh consecutive daily increase). Southern Omani-water routing now comprises ~45% of recorded movements, incorporating additional cleared non-hostile flags (including Taiwanese and Brazilian-owned tankers). Ghost-fleet Iranian oil shipments to China continue but represent a declining share of total flows. No attacks reported in the past 168 hours. The Trump administration issued a further 24-hour extension of the reprieve review (announced 9 April), referencing “verified protocol testing expansion and consistent transit gains” while upholding the demand for an open, free, and clear Strait. Iran-Oman joint monitoring protocol advanced with completion of a second incident-free monitored southern-route transit. War-risk premiums remain near 1% with the Chubb/US reinsurance facility actively utilized. Ras Laffan force majeure declaration and 3–5 year repair timeline (17% Qatar LNG capacity loss) are unchanged. Houthi Bab el-Mandeb signaling is unchanged and non-activated.

**Reference Classes and Base-Rate Prior**  
Reference classes (outside-in base rates before case-specific adjustment):  

1. **Iran-Iraq Tanker War (1980–88)**: Relevant for identical chokepoint attacks, insurance spikes, and export halts. Timeline to functional commercial recovery: 6–18+ months post-ceasefire once escorts and premiums aligned. Breaks down because modern coalition naval assets and satellite tracking allow faster threat suppression than in the 1980s. Suggests gradual long-term stabilization only.  

2. **2019–2020 Iranian tanker/Abqaiq attacks**: Relevant for short-duration Hormuz disruptions and temporary premium surges. Recovery: commercial volumes and insurance terms returned to baseline within 1–3 months after de-escalation. Breaks down due to far lower intensity and absence of state-on-state missile exchanges. Suggests modest short-term probabilities if fighting ends abruptly.  

3. **Red Sea Houthi crisis (2023–ongoing as of early 2026)**: Relevant for proxy-driven rerouting, elevated war-risk quotes, and partial export adjustments. Partial normalization: 6–12 months before premiums fell and schedules stabilized. Breaks down because scale was smaller and no direct Iranian state involvement. Suggests commercial recovery trails military calm by months.  

4. **1991 Gulf War**: Relevant for rapid kinetic phase followed by coalition naval clearance. Timeline: 1–3 months to restored transit and insurance norms. Breaks down because current conflict lacks decisive ground component or immediate regime outcome. Suggests faster recovery only under clear military resolution.  

5. **2003 Iraq War opening phase**: Relevant for Gulf-area port and export interruptions during regime-change fighting. Recovery: shipping and volumes normalized in 2–6 months once major combat subsided. Breaks down because Hormuz itself was never closed.  

**Base-rate prior** (timeline-based, pre-evidence):  
- 1 week: ~1%  
- 1 month: ~5%  
- 3 months: ~15–20%  
- 6 months: ~30–40%  
- 1 year: ~50–60%  
- 18 months: ~65–75%  

**Evidence Ledger**  

| Evidence Item | Source Type | Direction of Impact on Normalization | Confidence Level | Confirmed/Disputed/Inferred |
|---------------|-------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| Open transits reached 42 vessels on 8 April (seventh consecutive daily increase); southern Omani-water routing now ~45% of movements with additional non-hostile flags (Taiwanese/Brazilian tankers) | JMIC/Windward/UANI 7–9 Apr aggregates | Mildly toward (sustained momentum + routing share growth) but still strongly against (volumes ~69% below baseline) | High | Confirmed |
| Trump administration grants further 24-hour reprieve review extension citing “verified protocol testing expansion and consistent transit gains” (announced 9 April) | Reuters/Bloomberg/USNI 9 Apr | Mildly toward (extended window + explicit protocol reference) | High | Confirmed |
| Iran-Oman joint monitoring protocol completes second incident-free monitored southern-route transit | Omani Foreign Ministry/Al Arabiya 9 Apr | Mildly toward | High | Confirmed |
| No attacks reported in past 168 hours | UANI/CENTCOM-linked updates 6–9 Apr | Mildly toward (extended pause) | High | Confirmed |
| Ras Laffan 17% capacity loss, 3–5 year repairs, QatarEnergy force majeure unchanged | QatarEnergy/Rystad/Reuters ongoing | Strongly against | High | Confirmed |
| Houthi Bab el-Mandeb signaling unchanged and non-activated | Al Jazeera 8–9 Apr | Neutral | High | Confirmed |

**Key Drivers Toward Normalization** (ranked)  
1. Seventh consecutive daily transit increase with southern routing share reaching 45%.  
2. Additional 24-hour reprieve extension citing verified protocol testing expansion.  
3. Second successful monitored southern-route transit under joint protocol.  
4. 168-hour attack-free period.

**Key Drivers Against Normalization** (ranked)  
1. Volumes still ~69% below baseline with persistent safety-driven crew/P&I suppression.  
2. Binding 3–5 year Ras Laffan constraints and force majeure.  
3. Selective regime retention and ongoing ghost-fleet dominance.  
4. Houthi contingency posture unchanged.

**Decomposed Sub-Forecasts** (by horizon; key gating components)  
- Major reduction in direct strikes: 1 wk ~14%, 1 mo ~27%, 3 mo ~47%, 6 mo ~67%, 1 yr ~83%, 18 mo ~93%.  
- Sustained safe commercial transit (>80% levels): 1 wk ~5%, 1 mo ~11%, 3 mo ~20%, 6 mo ~38%, 1 yr ~58%, 18 mo ~74%.  
- Meaningful insurance normalization: lags transit; 1 wk ~3%, 1 mo ~9%, 3 mo ~17%, 6 mo ~33%, 1 yr ~53%, 18 mo ~68%.  
- Oil/LNG export recovery: gated by terminal restarts + transit; similar lag profile.  
- Proxy restraint + force drawdown + no new triggers: tracks direct-strike reduction but discounted by selective regime retention.

**Final Probability Forecasts by Horizon**  

**1 Week**  
• Probability: 5%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~1%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from seventh daily transit rise, routing share expansion to 45%, and 24-hour reprieve extension.  
• Core rationale: Day 44 shows continued incremental operational and diplomatic progress but volume/safety thresholds remain unmet; 30-day calm window still distant.  
• Main gating factor: Any vessel movement under active targeting.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Verified escorted convoy completion.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Reversal of reprieve extension or new strike.  
• Confidence in this estimate: High  

**1 Month**  
• Probability: 13%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~5%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from sustained transit momentum, second monitored transit, and extended review window.  
• Core rationale: Diplomatic and operational signals continue widening the window but insurance/transit behavioral lags dominate.  
• Main gating factor: Commercial transit volumes.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Routine escorted operations for 7+ days.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Collapse of reprieve review.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**3 Months**  
• Probability: 25%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~15–20%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Slight upward from extended attack-free period and protocol testing success.  
• Core rationale: De-escalation trajectory possible yet commercial/insurance recovery trails.  
• Main gating factor: 30-day safe-transit threshold.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Formal mediation breakthrough.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Infrastructure re-strike.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**6 Months**  
• Probability: 44%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~30–40%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Balanced; aligns with historical attrition despite suppression.  
• Core rationale: Interval supports capability degradation and partial rebound if kinetic phase subsides.  
• Main gating factor: Insurance quote stabilization.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Iranian internal pressure signals.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Entrenched proxy campaign.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**1 Year**  
• Probability: 63%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~50–60%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Upward from diplomatic channels and precedent.  
• Core rationale: Chokepoint cases historically normalize commercially inside one year post-peak.  
• Main gating factor: Export volume continuity.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Proxy settlement.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Fragmented post-conflict dynamics.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium-High  

**18 Months**  
• Probability: 80%  
• Base-rate anchor: ~65–75%  
• Current-evidence adjustment: Moderate upward; 60-day trigger window reachable.  
• Core rationale: Prolonged maritime conflicts achieve functional recovery; effects dissipate. Operational definition remains demanding because insurance, buyer behavior, and Ras Laffan repairs create multi-month lags even after kinetic calm.  
• Main gating factor: Absence of fresh escalation triggers.  
• What would raise this forecast materially: Coalition enforcement success.  
• What would lower this forecast materially: Persistent militia autonomy.  
• Confidence in this estimate: Medium  

**Most Likely Path**  
Transit momentum via selective regime and southern routes (now 45% share) builds through mid-April with reprieve review extension as immediate focal point; Oman protocol testing success likely enables expanded monitored transits by late April. Negotiated pause projected for July–August; commercial volumes and insurance terms follow with 8–12 week lag. Ras Laffan remains longest physical constraint; full Hormuz reopening projected for 9–13 months.

**Faster Normalization Case**  
Reprieve extension and protocol testing convert into operational escorts with measured compliance accepted. Insurer reinstatement by month 4. Scenario weight ~26%.

**Prolonged Instability Case**  
Reprieve review collapses and selective regime hardens; safety concerns and Houthi posture lock in disruption. Alternative routing entrenches; recovery to 14+ months. Scenario weight ~32%.

**Red-Team Critique**  
Overestimation risk if crew refusals and Ras Laffan repairs extend behavioral lag beyond recent transit and protocol momentum. Underestimation risk if reprieve extension and second monitored transit signal faster practical concessions than selective-regime history implies. Load-bearing assumptions include no Gulf-state direct entry and insurance lag capped at 3–4 months. Evidence on exact IRGC thresholds for regime adjustments remains indirect.

**Critical Signals to Monitor**  
- JMIC/Windward daily open-transit counts and southern-route share.  
- Outcome of Trump reprieve review post-24-hour extension.  
- Status of Iran-Oman protocol expanded testing phase.  
- QatarEnergy/Aramco volume and repair updates.  
- Lloyd’s Joint War Committee or Chubb reinsurance notices.  
- IEA export revisions, Brent 30-day volatility, and Houthi Bab el-Mandeb statements.

**Final Summary Table**  

Horizon | Probability | Main Gating Factor | Key Upside Trigger | Key Downside Trigger  
---|---|---|---|---  
1 Week | 5% | Active strikes/transit halt | Verified escorted convoy | Reversal of reprieve extension  
1 Month | 13% | Insurance + attacks | Routine escorted operations | Collapse of reprieve review  
3 Months | 25% | Transit recovery | Mediation breakthrough | Infrastructure re-strike  
6 Months | 44% | Export/insurance lag | Internal pressure | Proxy campaign  
1 Year | 63% | Volatility drop | Proxy settlement | Fragmented dynamics  
18 Months | 80% | No new triggers | Coalition success | Militia autonomy  

This forecast remains calibrated for operational use; commercial recovery continues to gate military pauses. Daily signals will drive recalibration.
